んだ.etymology: Colloquial explanatory sentence-ending construction ('it is that..., the thing is...'), contracted from のだ (*no da*), combining the clause-nominalizing particle の (> ん) + plain copula だ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — のだ
Wiktionary — のだ → んだ (Japanese)

アイシング.etymology: Borrowed from English *icing* ('sugar glaze or frosting applied to pastries and cakes', verbal noun from *ice*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アイシング
Wiktionary — アイシング (Japanese)

アップライトピアノ.etymology: Borrowed from English *upright piano* ('vertical-stringed piano', from *upright* + *piano*).

history.meaning: piano with vertical strings and soundboard

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アップライトピアノ
Wiktionary — アップライトピアノ (Japanese)

アーチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *arch* ('curved architectural structure spanning an opening'), ultimately from Old French *arche* and Latin *arcus* ('bow, arch').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — アーチ
Wiktionary — アーチ (Japanese)

アーモンド.etymology: Borrowed from English almond, tracing back through Old French almande to Greek ἀμυγδάλη (amygdálē).
アーモンド.notes: Ground almond meal (アーモンドプードル / アーモンド生地) is prized in Japanese pastry shops for tart crusts.

sources.title: Wiktionary — アーモンド (Japanese)

イニシャル.etymology: Borrowed from English *initial* ('first letter of a name'), ultimately from Latin *initiālis* ('of the beginning', from *initium* 'beginning').

history.meaning: first letter(s) of a person's name

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — イニシャル
Wiktionary — イニシャル (Japanese)

インク.etymology: Borrowed from English *ink* (alongside the older Dutch borrowing インキ from Dutch *inkt*), ultimately from Old French *enque* and Late Latin *encaustum*.

history.meaning: colored fluid used for writing and printing

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — インク
Wiktionary — インク (Japanese)

ウール.etymology: Borrowed from English *wool* ('fleece of sheep; woolen yarn or cloth'), from Old English *wull*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ウール
Wiktionary — ウール (Japanese)

エコー.etymology: Borrowed from English *echo* ('reflected sound; reverberation'), from Latin *ēchō* and Ancient Greek ἠχώ (*ēkhō* 'sound, echo').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — エコー
Wiktionary — エコー (Japanese)

エンジン.etymology: Borrowed from English *engine* ('mechanical motor'), from Old French *engin* and Latin *ingenium* ('innate talent, clever device').

history.meaning: motor converting energy into mechanical motion

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — エンジン
Wiktionary — エンジン (Japanese)

オクターブ.etymology: Borrowed from French/English octave, from Latin octāva ('eighth'), naming the eight-note span of a diatonic scale.
オクターブ.notes: Standard term across Japanese piano instruction and acoustics.

sources.title: Wiktionary — オクターブ (Japanese)

オフィス.etymology: Borrowed from English *office* ('place of business, workroom'), from Anglo-Norman/Old French *office* and Latin *officium* ('duty, service, office').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オフィス
Wiktionary — オフィス (Japanese)

オリーブオイル.etymology: Compound loanword from English olive oil (オリーブ + オイル).
オリーブオイル.notes: Coexists with older Sino-hybrid オリーブ油 (オリーブゆ) in home cooking and cafés.

sources.title: Wiktionary — オリーブオイル (Japanese)
Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オレンジジュース
Wiktionary — オレンジジュース (Japanese)

オーナー.etymology: Borrowed from English *owner* ('proprietor, one who owns a business or property', agent noun from *own*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オーナー
Wiktionary — オーナー (Japanese)

オーブン.etymology: Borrowed from English *oven* ('enclosed heated chamber for baking and roasting'), from Old English *ofn*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オーブン
Wiktionary — オーブン (Japanese)

オープン.etymology: Borrowed from English *open* ('unclosed, open for business, newly opened'), from Old English *open*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オープン
Wiktionary — オープン (Japanese)

カウンター.etymology: Borrowed from English *counter* ('long table or bar surface in a shop, café, or kitchen where customers are served'), from Anglo-Norman *countour* ('counting-house desk') and Latin *computāre*.

history.meaning: counter (in a café, bakery, or reception)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カウンター
Wiktionary — カウンター (Japanese)

カウントダウン.etymology: Borrowed from English *countdown* ('counting backward to zero to mark the start of an event', from *count* + *down*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カウントダウン
Wiktionary — カウントダウン (Japanese)

カチッ.etymology: Onomatopoeic adverb written in katakana with a final glottal stop (ッ), imitating the crisp, metallic or hard-plastic click of a latch, timer, or switch engaging ('click!, snap!').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かちっと
Wiktionary — かちっと (Japanese)

カチッと.etymology: Onomatopoeic adverb formed from カチッ ('click!') + quotative/adverbial particle と, describing a switch, lock, or mechanism clicking cleanly into place ('with a crisp click').

history.meaning: with a sharp click; firmly in place

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — かちっと
Wiktionary — カチッと (かちっと) (Japanese)

カップ.etymology: Borrowed from English *cup* ('small handled drinking vessel for tea or coffee; measuring cup'), from Late Latin *cuppa* ('drinking vessel'). Contrasts in Japanese with コップ (from Dutch/Portuguese *kop*, usually a handleless glass tumbler).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カップ
Wiktionary — カップ (Japanese)

カフェ.etymology: Borrowed from French café ('coffeehouse'), first popularized in late Meiji and Taishō cities and revived in contemporary Japanese for neighborhood coffeehouses.

sources.title: Wiktionary — カフェ (Japanese)

カモミールティー.etymology: Compound loanword from English *chamomile tea* (combining *chamomile*, from Greek χαμαίμηλον *khamaimēlon* 'earth-apple', + *tea*).

history.meaning: herbal infusion made from chamomile flowers

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カモミール
Wiktionary — カモミール (Japanese)

カーテン.etymology: Borrowed from English *curtain* ('hanging window drapery'), from Old French *cortine* and Late Latin *cortīna*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カーテン
Wiktionary — カーテン (Japanese)

カーディガン.etymology: Borrowed from English *cardigan* ('knitted sweater opening down the front with buttons'), named after James Brudenell, 7th Earl of Cardigan (1797–1868), whose troops wore knitted waistcoats during the Crimean War.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カーディガン
Wiktionary — カーディガン (Japanese)

カード.etymology: Borrowed from English *card* ('stiff rectangular piece of paper or plastic'), from Old French *carte* and Latin *charta* ('papyrus leaf, paper').

history.meaning: message card, index card, or payment card

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カード
Wiktionary — カード (Japanese)

ガラス.etymology: Borrowed in the Edo period from Dutch glas ('glass'), referring to sheet and window glass as a material (whereas the later English borrowing グラス denotes a drinking glass).

sources.title: Wiktionary — ガラス (Japanese)

ガラス瓶.etymology: Hybrid compound noun ガラス瓶 ('glass bottle, glass jar'), combining Edo-period Dutch loanword ガラス (from Dutch *glas* 'glass') + Sino-Japanese 瓶 (びん 'bottle, jar', from Middle Chinese *beng*).

history.form: ガラス (硝子) + 瓶 (びん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 硝子瓶
Wiktionary — ガラス瓶 (Japanese)

ガーデンカフェ.etymology: Compound loanword combining English *garden* (ガーデン) + French/English *café* (カフェ), referring to a café with an outdoor garden terrace.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カフェ
Wiktionary — カフェ (Japanese)

キッチン.etymology: Borrowed from English *kitchen* ('room equipped for preparing and cooking food'), from Old English *cyċene* and Vulgar Latin *cocīna*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — キッチン
Wiktionary — キッチン (Japanese)

クッション.etymology: Borrowed from English cushion, from Old French coissin.
クッション.notes: Refers to soft seat cushions on wooden café chairs as well as mechanical shock-absorbing pads.

sources.title: Wiktionary — クッション (Japanese)

クリーム色.etymology: Hybrid color compound クリーム色 ('cream color, pale yellowish-white'), combining English loanword クリーム (from English *cream*) + native Japanese 色 (いろ 'color, hue').

history.meaning: pale yellowish-white color of dairy cream

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — クリーム色
Wiktionary — クリーム + 色 (いろ) (Japanese)

クルミ材.etymology: Hybrid woodworking compound クルミ材 ('walnut wood, walnut timber'), combining native Japanese クルミ (胡桃 'walnut tree') + Sino-Japanese 材 (ざい 'timber, lumber, material').

history.form: クルミ (胡桃) + 材 (ざい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 胡桃
Wiktionary — 胡桃 (Japanese)

クロス.etymology: Borrowed from two converging English words: (1) English *cloth* ('woven fabric, tablecloth', as in テーブルクロス), and (2) English *cross* ('intersecting lines, cross shape'). In café and interior contexts it commonly denotes a tablecloth or wiping cloth.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — クロス
Wiktionary — クロス (Japanese)

グラニュー糖.etymology: Hybrid Meiji culinary compound clipping English granulated (sugar) to グラニュー and attaching Sino-Japanese 糖 (とう, 'sugar').
グラニュー糖.notes: Refers to fine, dry, free-flowing white crystals prized in pastry baking.

sources.title: Wiktionary — グラニュー糖 (Japanese)
Wiktionary — ケーキ (Japanese)

コク.etymology: Culinary and sensory noun コク (originally written 濃く or 酷 'richness, body, depth of flavor'), derived from the Sino-Japanese noun 酷 (*koku* 'intense, ripe to the fullest degree', or the adverbial stem 濃く *koku* of 濃い 'thick, rich, strong'). Often written in katakana in modern food writing.

history.meaning: full-bodied ripeness and depth of taste in sake or broth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — こく
Wiktionary — コク (Japanese)

コップ.etymology: Borrowed from Dutch kop (or Portuguese copo) during the early modern trade era to name a tumbler or drinking cup without a handle.

sources.title: Wiktionary — コップ (Japanese)
Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コンサートホール
Wiktionary — コンサートホール (Japanese)

コンロ.etymology: Edo-period Sino-Japanese kitchen word 焜炉 (こんろ, combining 焜 'bright flame' + 炉 'hearth/brazier'), influenced in use by Dutch komfoor ('portable brazier').
コンロ.notes: Today written in katakana コンロ for gas and induction kitchen stoves.

sources.title: Wiktionary — コンロ (Japanese)

コート.etymology: Borrowed from English *coat* ('outer garment worn for warmth; layer of paint/glaze'), from Old French *cote* ('tunic, coat'); or homophonous English *court* ('sports court').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コート
Wiktionary — コート (Japanese)

コーナー.etymology: Borrowed from English *corner* ('angle where two walls or streets meet; specialized section in a shop or room'), from Anglo-Norman *cornere* and Latin *cornū* ('horn, projecting point').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーナー
Wiktionary — コーナー (Japanese)

コーヒー.etymology: Borrowed in the late Edo period from Dutch koffie ('coffee') through the Dutch trading post at Dejima in Nagasaki; scholars also coined the phonetic kanji spelling 珈琲.

sources.title: Wiktionary — コーヒー (Japanese)

コーヒーカップ.etymology: Borrowed from English *coffee cup* (combining Dutch/English loanword コーヒー 'coffee' + English カップ 'cup').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーヒーカップ
Wiktionary — コーヒーカップ (Japanese)

コーヒーマシン.etymology: Borrowed from English *coffee machine* (combining コーヒー 'coffee' + English マシン 'machine, automated appliance').

history.meaning: appliance for brewing espresso or coffee

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — コーヒー
Wiktionary — コーヒー (Japanese)

サイズ.etymology: Borrowed from English *size* ('dimensions, magnitude, garment/portion measurement'), shortened in Middle English from *assize* ('fixed standard or measure', from Old French *assise*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サイズ
Wiktionary — サイズ (Japanese)

サイン.etymology: Borrowed from English *sign* ('mark, symbol, signal, signboard'), from Old French *signe* and Latin *signum*. In Japanese usage it also commonly means a handwritten 'signature' or 'autograph'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サイン
Wiktionary — サイン (Japanese)

サンルーム.etymology: Borrowed from English *sunroom* ('glass-enclosed porch or room admitting abundant sunlight', from *sun* + *room*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サンルーム
Wiktionary — サンルーム (Japanese)

サービス.etymology: Borrowed from English *service* ('hospitality, assistance to customers'), from Old French *servise* and Latin *servitium*. In Japanese commercial usage it also developed the sense 'complimentary item, free extra, discount'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サービス
Wiktionary — サービス (Japanese)

シェフ.etymology: Borrowed from French chef (short for chef de cuisine, 'head of the kitchen').
シェフ.notes: Used both as a standalone noun and as a warm respectful title after a baker's or cook's name.

sources.title: Wiktionary — シェフ (Japanese)

シナモン.etymology: Borrowed from English *cinnamon* ('aromatic inner bark of *Cinnamomum* trees used as a spice'), ultimately via Old French, Latin, and Greek κιννάμωμον (*kinnámōmon*) from a Semitic source.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモン
Wiktionary — シナモン (Japanese)

シナモンパン.etymology: Hybrid bakery compound ('cinnamon bread / cinnamon bun'), combining English loanword シナモン (*cinnamon*) + Portuguese loanword パン (from Portuguese *pão* 'bread', introduced in the 16th century).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモン
Wiktionary — パン (Japanese)

シナモンロール.etymology: Borrowed from English *cinnamon roll* ('spiraled sweet pastry seasoned with cinnamon and sugar', from *cinnamon* + *roll*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモンロール
Wiktionary — シナモンロール (Japanese)

シャッター.etymology: Borrowed from English *shutter* ('hinged or rolling window/shop-front cover; camera shutter', agent noun from *shut*).

history.meaning: rolling shop shutter; window shutter; camera shutter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シャッター
Wiktionary — シャッター (Japanese)

シャツ.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English *shirts* (plural of *shirt*, reanalyzed in Japanese as a singular noun), from Old English *scyrte*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シャツ
Wiktionary — シャツ (Japanese)

シャワー.etymology: Borrowed from English shower (short for shower bath).

sources.title: Wiktionary — シャワー (Japanese)

シンプル.etymology: Borrowed from English *simple* ('plain, uncomplicated, unadorned'), from Old French *simple* and Latin *simplex* ('single-fold, plain'). Used in Japanese as a *na*-adjective praising clean, uncluttered design.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シンプル
Wiktionary — シンプル (Japanese)

シーツ.etymology: Borrowed from English *sheets* (plural of *sheet* 'bedsheet', adopted as a singular noun in Japanese), from Old English *scīete* ('piece of linen cloth').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シーツ
Wiktionary — シーツ (Japanese)

ジャム.etymology: Borrowed from English *jam* ('sweet fruit preserve boiled with sugar'), introduced into Japanese culinary vocabulary in the Meiji period.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ジャム
Wiktionary — ジャム (Japanese)

ジャムパン.etymology: Japanese bakery compound ('jam bun, bread roll filled with fruit jam'), first created in Tokyo in 1900 by Kimura-ya Bakery, combining English loanword ジャム (*jam*) + Portuguese loanword パン (*pão* 'bread').

history.meaning: sweet bread roll filled with fruit jam

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ジャムパン
Wiktionary — ジャムパン (Japanese)

スイッチ.etymology: Borrowed from English 'switch', a device that turns an electric current on and off; Japanese also uses it for railway points and, as スイッチする, for changing one's approach.

sources.title: Wiktionary — スイッチ (Japanese)

スクランブルエッグ.etymology: Borrowed from English *scrambled eggs* (with the plural *-s* and past-participle *-d* dropped in Japanese phonetic adaptation).

history.meaning: eggs beaten and pan-cooked while stirring

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スクランブルエッグ
Wiktionary — スクランブルエッグ (Japanese)

スケッチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *sketch* ('rough drawing or outline'), from Dutch *schets* and Italian *schizzo* (ultimately from Latin *schedius* and Greek σχέδιος 'done offhand').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スケッチ
Wiktionary — スケッチ (Japanese)

スピーチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *speech* ('formal address or talk delivered to an audience'), from Old English *spǣċ*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スピーチ
Wiktionary — スピーチ (Japanese)

スプーン.etymology: Borrowed from English *spoon* ('utensil with a shallow bowl on a handle'), from Old English *spōn* ('chip or sliver of wood').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スプーン
Wiktionary — スプーン (Japanese)

スポンジ.etymology: Borrowed from English sponge, ultimately from Ancient Greek σπογγιά (spongiá).
スポンジ.notes: Used both for kitchen/window sponges and sponge cake (スポンジケーキ).

sources.title: Wiktionary — スポンジ (Japanese)

スーツケース.etymology: Borrowed from English suitcase ('flat-sided Rectangular travel bag'), combining スーツ ('suit') and ケース ('case').

sources.title: Wiktionary — スーツケース (Japanese)

スープ.etymology: Borrowed from English *soup* (and French *soupe*), referring mainly to Western-style or Chinese-style soups in contrast to traditional Japanese 汁 (しる / みそ汁).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スープ
Wiktionary — スープ (Japanese)

セット.etymology: Borrowed from English *set* ('matched group of items; setting up equipment or hair; fixed-menu combination').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — セット
Wiktionary — セット (Japanese)

セリフ.etymology: Native Edo-period theatrical noun 台詞・科白 (せりふ 'actor's spoken lines on stage, remark'), derived from 競り言ふ (*seri-iu* 'speaking in turn / vying in speech') or 世流布 (*serufu*). Often written in katakana セリフ in modern prose.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 台詞
Wiktionary — セリフ (Japanese)

センチ.etymology: Clipped loanword from French *centimètre* / English *centimeter* (センチメートル 'centimeter, one-hundredth of a meter', from Latin *centum* 'hundred' + *mètre*). Also used as a clipping of センチメンタル (*sentimental*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — センチ
Wiktionary — センチ (Japanese)

セーター.etymology: Borrowed from English *sweater* ('knitted pullover garment', originally athletic wear designed to induce sweating, from *sweat* + *-er*), with simplification of the *sw-* cluster to *s-* in Japanese.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — セーター
Wiktionary — セーター (Japanese)

ゼロ.etymology: Borrowed from French *zéro* / English *zero* ('the number 0, nothing'), ultimately via Italian *zero* and Medieval Latin *zephirum* from Arabic صِفْر (*ṣifr* 'empty, zero').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ゼロ
Wiktionary — ゼロ (Japanese)

タイマー.etymology: Borrowed from English *timer* ('device that measures elapsed time and signals when a set interval ends', agent noun from *time*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タイマー
Wiktionary — タイマー (Japanese)

タイヤ.etymology: Borrowed from English *tire* / *tyre* ('rubber covering placed around a wheel rim').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タイヤ
Wiktionary — タイヤ (Japanese)

タオル.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English *towel* ('absorbent cloth for drying'), from Old French *toaille*. Primarily denotes Western-style looped cotton terrycloth towels in contrast to flat woven 手拭い (*tenugui*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タオル
Wiktionary — タオル (Japanese)

タクシー.etymology: Borrowed in the Taishō era from English taxi, itself clipped from taximeter cab.

sources.title: Wiktionary — タクシー (Japanese)

タブレット.etymology: Borrowed from English *tablet* ('flat portable touchscreen computer; compressed medicinal pill or lozenge'), from Old French *tablete* ('small table or writing slate').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タブレット
Wiktionary — タブレット (Japanese)

タルト.etymology: Borrowed from French *tarte* (and English *tart*), referring to a baked shortcrust pastry shell filled with fruit, custard, or cream; ultimately from Old French *tarte*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タルト
Wiktionary — タルト (Japanese)

タルト生地.etymology: Hybrid baking compound タルト生地 ('tart dough, shortcrust pastry dough'), combining French loanword タルト (*tarte*) + native/Sino-Japanese 生地 (きじ 'unworked material, dough, fabric', from 生 *ki* 'raw, natural' + 地 *ji* 'ground, base material').

history.meaning: pastry dough for a tart shell

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 生地
Wiktionary — 生地 (Japanese)

チェックイン.etymology: Borrowed from English *check-in* / *check in* ('registering one's arrival at a hotel, inn, or airport').

history.meaning: registration upon arrival at a hotel or airport

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — チェックイン
Wiktionary — チェックイン (Japanese)

チョーク.etymology: Borrowed from English *chalk* ('soft white limestone or calcium sulfate stick used for writing on blackboards'), from Old English *cealc* and Latin *calx* ('lime').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — チョーク
Wiktionary — チョーク (Japanese)
Wiktionary — チーズ (Japanese)
Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ティーカップ
Wiktionary — ティーカップ (Japanese)

テーブル.etymology: Borrowed from English table to name a raised dining or café table used with chairs, in contrast with low floor tables.

sources.title: Wiktionary — テーブル (Japanese)

history.meaning: cloth spread over a dining or café table

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — テーブルクロス
Wiktionary — テーブルクロス (Japanese)

テープ.etymology: Borrowed from English *tape* ('narrow strip of adhesive cloth/plastic, ribbon, or magnetic recording strip'), from Old English *tæppe* ('strip of cloth').

history.meaning: adhesive strip, ribbon, or recording tape

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — テープ
Wiktionary — テープ (Japanese)

デシベル.etymology: Borrowed from English *decibel* (and French *décibel*), the logarithmic unit of sound intensity combining metric prefix *deci-* ('one-tenth', from Latin *decimus*) + *bel* (named in honor of telephone pioneer Alexander Graham Bell).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — デシベル
Wiktionary — デシベル (Japanese)

トマト.etymology: Borrowed from English *tomato*, which came via Spanish *tomate* from Nahuatl *tomatl* ('swelling fruit'). Introduced to Japan as an ornamental plant in the Edo period (called 赤茄子 *akanasu*) and popularized as a food crop under the name トマト in the Meiji–Taishō era.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トマト
Wiktionary — トマト (Japanese)

トラック.etymology: Borrowed from two converging English words: (1) American English *truck* ('motor vehicle for hauling freight'), and (2) English *track* ('running track, path, or recorded audio track').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トラック
Wiktionary — トラック (Japanese)

トレイ.etymology: Borrowed from English tray, tracing back to Old English trīg ('wooden board or shallow dish').
トレイ.notes: Also spelled トレー; standard word in cafés and bakeries for baking and serving trays.

sources.title: Wiktionary — トレイ (Japanese)

トースト.etymology: Borrowed from English *toast* ('sliced bread browned by radiant heat'), from Old French *toster* ('to roast, grill') and Latin *tostus* ('parched, roasted').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トースト
Wiktionary — トースト (Japanese)

ト長調.etymology: Meiji-era Japanese musical terminology ('G major'), combining ト (the 7th symbol of the traditional *iroha* syllabary, assigned in Japanese music theory to the 5th scale degree / pitch G, equivalent to Western A–B–C–D–E–F–G mapped to イ–ロ–ハ–ニ–ホ–ヘ–ト) + Sino-Japanese 長調 (ちょうちょう 'major key', from 長 'major/long' + 調 'key, mode').

history.form: ト (iroha note G) + 長調 (major key)
ト長調 (とちょうちょう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ト長調
Wiktionary — ト長調 (とちょうちょう) (Japanese)

ド.etymology: Borrowed from Italian solfège syllable *do* ('the first note of the diatonic scale, C in fixed-do'), introduced in 17th-century Italy (replacing Guido of Arezzo's *ut*) and adopted into Japanese music education in the Meiji period.

history.meaning: first degree of the scale; pitch C

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ド
Wiktionary — ド (Japanese)

ドア.etymology: Borrowed from English door, referring specifically to a hinged or automatic Western-style door rather than a sliding Japanese 戸 (to) or 襖 (fusuma).

sources.title: Wiktionary — ドア (Japanese)

ドキドキ.etymology: Katakana orthographic spelling of the reduplicated mimetic word どきどき, imitating the rapid thumping or pounding of the heart from excitement, suspense, or nervousness.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どきどき
Wiktionary — どきどき (Japanese)

ドライバー.etymology: Borrowed from English *driver*, functioning in Japanese both as a clipping of *screwdriver* ('hand tool for turning screws') and in the sense of 'motor vehicle driver'.

history.meaning: tool for driving screws; vehicle driver

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ドライバー
Wiktionary — ドライバー (Japanese)

ナプキン.etymology: Borrowed from English *napkin* ('square of cloth or paper used at table to wipe the lips and fingers'), from Middle English *napekyn* (diminutive of Old French *nape* 'tablecloth', from Latin *mappa*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ナプキン
Wiktionary — ナプキン (Japanese)

ニュース.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English *news* ('tidings, report of recent events', calqued on Old French *noveles* / Medieval Latin *nova* 'new things').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ニュース
Wiktionary — ニュース (Japanese)
Wiktionary — ネクタイ (Japanese)

レシート.etymology: Borrowed from English *receipt* ('printed slip acknowledging payment for goods or services'), from Anglo-Norman *receite* and Latin *recepta* ('received').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レシート
Wiktionary — レシート (Japanese)

レジ.etymology: Clipped Japanese loanword from English *register* (specifically キャッシュ・レジスター *cash register* > レジスター > レジ), denoting both the cash register machine and the checkout counter.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レジ
Wiktionary — レジ (Japanese)

レッスン.etymology: Borrowed from English *lesson* ('instructional session or practice period, especially in music, art, or sports'), from Old French *leçon* and Latin *lēctiō* ('reading').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レッスン
Wiktionary — レッスン (Japanese)
Wiktionary — レモン (Japanese)

レモンカード.etymology: Borrowed from English *lemon curd* ('thick, smooth, tangy spread cooked from lemon juice, zest, butter, eggs, and sugar', combining *lemon* + *curd*).

history.meaning: creamy citrus dessert spread and tart filling

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レモン
Wiktionary — レモン (Japanese)

レモンケーキ.etymology: Borrowed from English *lemon cake* (combining *lemon* + *cake*; in Japan also associated since the Shōwa era with lemon-shaped sponge cakes glazed with lemon-flavored white chocolate).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レモン
Wiktionary — ケーキ (Japanese)

レモンシュガー.etymology: Borrowed from English *lemon sugar* ('sugar infused or mixed with grated lemon zest or lemon flavor', combining *lemon* + *sugar*).

history.meaning: lemon-scented sugar for baking and tea

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レモン
Wiktionary — レモン (Japanese)

レモンタルト.etymology: Compound pastry term ('lemon tart'), combining English loanword レモン (*lemon*) + French loanword タルト (*tarte* 'tart').

history.meaning: pastry tart filled with lemon curd/cream

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タルト
Wiktionary — タルト (Japanese)

レンガ.etymology: Sino-Japanese architectural compound 煉瓦 (れんが 'fired clay brick'), coined/popularized in late Edo and Meiji Japan from 煉 ('knead and temper with fire') + 瓦 ('kiln-fired clay tile'). Frequently written in katakana レンガ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 煉瓦
Wiktionary — レンガ (Japanese)

レンズ.etymology: Borrowed in the late Edo period via Dutch *lens* and reinforced by English *lens* ('curved piece of polished glass for focusing light'), ultimately from Latin *lēns* ('lentil', from the biconvex shape of a lentil seed).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レンズ
Wiktionary — レンズ (Japanese)

レンズ豆.etymology: Partial calque combining English/German loan レンズ ('lens', ultimately from Latin lēns, 'lentil') with native 豆 (まめ, 'bean, pulse').
レンズ豆.notes: Optics borrowed Latin lēns ('lentil') for glass lenses because of their curved lentil shape, and Japanese named the legume 'lens-bean' in turn!

sources.title: Wiktionary — レンズ豆 (Japanese)

レンチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *wrench* ('spanner tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts', from Old English *wrenc* 'twisting').

history.meaning: tool for turning bolts and nuts

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レンチ
Wiktionary — レンチ (Japanese)

レース.etymology: Borrowed from two English homophones: (1) English *lace* ('delicate openwork fabric of threads', from Old French *las* 'noose, cord' and Latin *laqueus*), as in レースのカーテン ('lace curtains'), and (2) English *race* ('speed competition').

history.meaning: delicate openwork fabric / competition of speed

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — レース
Wiktionary — レース (Japanese)

ロビー.etymology: Borrowed from English *lobby* ('spacious entrance hall or waiting foyer in a hotel, inn, or concert hall'), from Medieval Latin *lobia* ('covered walk, gallery').

history.meaning: foyer or reception hall of a building

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ロビー
Wiktionary — ロビー (Japanese)

ワルツ.etymology: Borrowed from English *waltz* (and German *Walzer* 'ballroom dance and musical composition in triple 3/4 time', from German *walzen* 'to revolve, glide').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ワルツ
Wiktionary — ワルツ (Japanese)

ワンピース.etymology: Borrowed from English *one-piece (dress)*, referring in Japanese since the Taishō/Shōwa period to a woman's one-piece dress (whose bodice and skirt form a single garment).

history.meaning: dress made as a single garment

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ワンピース
Wiktionary — ワンピース (Japanese)

一.etymology: Numeral 一 ('one'), read either with the Sino-Japanese borrowing いち / いつ (from Middle Chinese *'jit* 'one') or with the native Japanese root ひと (*pito* 'one').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一
Wiktionary — 一 (Japanese)

一つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pitotu* (一つ 'one thing, one'), composed of the native numeral root ひと- (一 *pito* 'one') + the native general classifier suffix -つ (*-tu*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一つ
Wiktionary — 一つ (Japanese)

一つ星.etymology: Native Japanese compound 一つ星 (ひとつぼし 'a single star; one-star rating'), combining 一つ (ひとつ 'one') + 星 (ほし > ぼし via rendaku, 'star', from Old Japanese *posi*). Originally denoting the evening star shining alone at dusk, and now also calquing culinary/hotel 'one-star' ratings.

history.meaning: solitary star in the evening sky

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一つ星
Wiktionary — 一つ星 (Japanese)

一つ目.etymology: Ordinal numeral compound 一つ目 (ひとつめ 'the first one'), formed by attaching the ordinal/sequential suffix -目 (め, originally 'eye, notch on a measuring scale') to 一つ (ひとつ 'one').

history.meaning: the first item (also 'one-eyed' as a noun)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一つ目
Wiktionary — ひとつめ (一つ目) (Japanese)

一オクターブ.etymology: Hybrid musical measurement compound ('one octave'), combining Sino-Japanese numeral 一 (いち 'one') + loanword オクターブ (from French/English *octave*, ultimately from Latin *octāva* 'eighth degree of the diatonic scale').

history.form: 一 (いち) + オクターブ
history.meaning: an interval of one octave (eight diatonic degrees)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — オクターブ
Wiktionary — オクターブ (Japanese)

一ダース.etymology: Hybrid numeral-classifier compound ('one dozen, twelve items'), combining Sino-Japanese numeral 一 (いち 'one') + Meiji-era English loanword ダース (from English *dozen*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ダース
Wiktionary — ダース (Japanese)

一ミリ.etymology: Hybrid metric measurement compound ('one millimeter; a tiny bit'), combining Sino-Japanese numeral 一 (いち 'one') + clipped loanword ミリ (from *millimètre / millimeter*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ミリ
Wiktionary — ミリ (Japanese)

一人.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pitori* (一人 'one person, alone, by oneself'), composed of the native numeral root ひと- (一 *pito* 'one') + the native human classifier suffix -り (*-ri*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一人
Wiktionary — 一人 (ひとり) (Japanese)

一体.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 一体 (いったい), from 一 ('one') + 体 ('body, form, substance'). Originally a Buddhist and philosophical noun meaning 'one body, a single whole', in Early Modern Japanese it also grammaticalized into an emphatic interrogative adverb ('what on earth?, in the world').

history.meaning: one body; (in questions) what/who on earth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一体
Wiktionary — 一体 (Japanese)

一個.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一個 (いっこ 'one piece, one small object'), combining 一 (いち > いっ 'one') + counter 個 (こ, originally a tally of bamboo stalks in Chinese, generalized to small discrete objects).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一個
Wiktionary — 一個 (いっこ) (Japanese)

一円.etymology: Sino-Japanese monetary compound 一円 (いちえん 'one yen'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + 円 (えん 'circle, round coin; yen', adopted in 1871 as Japan's modern decimal currency unit after round silver coins).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一円
Wiktionary — 一円 (いちえん) (Japanese)

一分.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一分 (いっぷん 'one minute', or いちぶ 'one-tenth, one part'), combining 一 ('one') + 分 ('minute of time; fraction/tenth', from 'dividing an hour into sixty parts').

history.form: 一分 (いっぷん / いちぶ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一分
Wiktionary — 一分 (いっぷん / いちぶ) (Japanese)

一切れ.etymology: Native Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一切れ (ひときれ 'one slice, one piece, one cut'), combining ひと- (一 'one') + 切れ (きれ, nominalized stem of 切る *kiru* 'to cut, slice').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一切れ
Wiktionary — ひときれ (一切れ) (Japanese)

一口.etymology: Native Japanese compound 一口 (ひとくち 'one bite, one mouthful, a sip, a brief word'), combining ひと- (一 'one') + 口 (くち 'mouth, opening, share').

history.meaning: one bite; one sip; one share

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一口
Wiktionary — 一口 (Japanese)

一台.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一台 (いちだい 'one machine, appliance, vehicle, or piano'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + counter 台 (だい 'platform, stand, mounted apparatus').

history.meaning: one vehicle, machine, or large instrument

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一台
Wiktionary — 一台 (いちだい) (Japanese)

一回.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一回 (いっかい 'once, one time, first round/inning'), combining 一 (いち > いっ 'one') + counter 回 (かい 'revolving turn, occurrence').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一回
Wiktionary — 一回 (いっかい) (Japanese)

一巻.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一巻 (いっかん / ひとまき 'one roll, one spool [of tape/film], Volume One'), combining 一 ('one') + 巻 ('scroll, roll, volume').

history.form: 一巻 (いっかん / ひとまき)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一巻
Wiktionary — 一巻 (いっかん / ひとまき) (Japanese)

一度.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 一度 (いちど 'once, one time; one degree'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + 度 (ど 'time, occasion, degree', alongside native ひとたび).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一度
Wiktionary — 一度 (いちど) (Japanese)

一度目.etymology: Ordinal compound 一度目 (いちどめ 'the first time'), formed by attaching the native ordinal suffix -目 (め) to 一度 (いちど 'one time').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一度
Wiktionary — 一度 (Japanese)

一日中.etymology: Temporal compound 一日中 (いちにちじゅう 'all day long, throughout the whole day'), combining 一日 (いちにち 'one day') + Sino-Japanese suffix -中 (じゅう 'throughout the entire span of').

history.form: 一日中 (いちにちじゅう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一日中
Wiktionary — 一日中 (いちにちじゅう) (Japanese)

一時間.etymology: Sino-Japanese temporal duration compound 一時間 (いちじかん 'one hour'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + 時間 (じかん 'hour, span of time', from 時 'hour/time' + 間 'interval').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一時間
Wiktionary — 一時間 (いちじかん) (Japanese)

一時間ごと.etymology: Distributive temporal phrase 一時間ごと (いちじかんごと 'every hour, hourly'), combining 一時間 ('one hour') + native distributive suffix -ごと (毎 'every, each').

history.form: 一時間 (いちじかん) + ごと (毎)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一時間
Wiktionary — 毎 (Japanese)

一晩.etymology: Hybrid temporal compound 一晩 (ひとばん 'one night, overnight'), combining native numeral prefix ひと- (一 'one') + Sino-Japanese 晩 (ばん 'evening, night').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一晩
Wiktionary — ひとばん (一晩) (Japanese)

一晩中.etymology: Temporal compound 一晩中 (ひとばんじゅう 'all night long, throughout the night'), combining 一晩 (ひとばん 'one night') + suffix -中 (じゅう 'throughout').

history.form: ひとばんじゅう (一晩中)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一晩
Wiktionary — 一晩 (Japanese)

一本.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一本 (いっぽん 'one long cylindrical object, bottle, tree, street, or phone call'), combining 一 (いち > いっ 'one') + counter 本 (ほん > ぽん 'tree trunk, long slender item').

history.meaning: one long cylindrical object (bottle, pen, street, etc.)

morphemes.meaning: counter for long slender items or bottles

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一本
Wiktionary — 一本 (いっぽん) (Japanese)

一枚.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一枚 (いちまい 'one flat thin object, sheet, plate, or garment'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + counter 枚 (まい, originally 'stem/board' in Chinese, used since Old/Early Middle Japanese for flat items).

history.meaning: one flat sheet, plate, board, or cloth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一枚
Wiktionary — 一枚 (いちまい) (Japanese)

一枚目.etymology: Ordinal compound 一枚目 (いちまいめ 'the first sheet, page, or slice'), formed by attaching the native ordinal suffix -目 (め) to 一枚 (いちまい 'one flat item').

history.meaning: the first sheet, plate, or slice

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一枚
Wiktionary — 一枚 (Japanese)

一滴.etymology: Numeral-classifier compound 一滴 (いってき / ひとしずく 'one drop of liquid'), combining 一 ('one') + 滴 ('drop, trickle').

history.form: 一滴 (いってき / ひとしずく)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一滴
Wiktionary — 一滴 (いってき / ひとしずく) (Japanese)

一番.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 一番 (いちばん), from 一 ('one, first') + 番 ('turn on watch, numbered order'). Originally meaning 'the first turn on guard or in a contest', it grammaticalized into the standard superlative adverb ('most, number one, best').

history.meaning: first turn; number one in order

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一番
Wiktionary — 一番 (Japanese)

一秒.etymology: Sino-Japanese temporal compound 一秒 (いちびょう 'one second'), combining 一 (いち 'one') + 秒 (びょう, originally 'the fine beard/awn on a grain of rice', adopted in East Asian astronomy and clockwork for 'one-sixtieth of a minute').

history.meaning: one second of time or arc

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一秒
Wiktionary — 一秒 (いちびょう) (Japanese)

一緒.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 一緒 (いっしょ 'together, at the same time, identical'), originally written 一処 ('one and the same place', from 一 'one' + 処 'place') in medieval texts, and later re-spelled 一緒 ('one thread/lineage').

history.meaning: together; at the same time; the same

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一緒
Wiktionary — 一緒 (いっしょ) (Japanese)

一袋.etymology: Native Japanese numeral-classifier compound 一袋 (ひとふくろ 'one bag, one sackful, one pouch'), combining ひと- (一 'one') + 袋 (ふくろ 'bag, sack, pouch', from Old Japanese *pukuro*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一袋
Wiktionary — ひとふくろ (一袋) (Japanese)

一言.etymology: Native Japanese compound 一言 (ひとこと 'a single word, a brief remark'), combining ひと- (一 'one') + 言 (こと 'word, speech', from Old Japanese *koto*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一言
Wiktionary — 一言 (Japanese)

一言一句.etymology: Four-character Sino-Japanese idiom (四字熟語) 一言一句 (いちごんいっく), pairing 一言 ('a single word') and 一句 ('a single phrase').
一言一句.notes: Uses traditional go'on reading ごん for 言 in set classical expressions.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 一言一句 (Japanese)

一週間.etymology: Sino-Japanese temporal duration compound 一週間 (いっしゅうかん 'one week'), combining 一 (いち > いっ 'one') + 週 ('seven-day cycle/week', popularized in the Meiji period) + 間 (かん 'duration, interval').

history.form: 一週間 (いっしゅうかん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一週間
Wiktionary — 一週間 (いっしゅうかん) (Japanese)

一階.etymology: Sino-Japanese architectural compound 一階 (いっかい 'first floor, ground floor'), combining 一 (いち > いっ 'one') + 階 (かい 'stairs, story/floor of a building').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一階
Wiktionary — 一階 (いっかい) (Japanese)

一音.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 一音 (いちおん / ひとおと 'a single musical note, single sound, or syllable'), combining 一 ('one') + 音 ('sound, musical note').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 一音
Wiktionary — 一音 (いちおん) (Japanese)

丁寧.etymology: Sino-Japanese adjectival noun 丁寧 (ていねい 'polite, courteous, careful, thorough'). In ancient China 丁寧 (originally 丁口/鉦) denoted a bronze percussion gong struck repeatedly to warn troops, shifting to 'repeated earnest instructions' and in Japanese to 'attentive, painstaking, polite'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 丁寧
Wiktionary — 丁寧 (ていねい) (Japanese)

七.etymology: Numeral 七 ('seven'), read either with the native Japanese root なな (*nana* 'seven', from Old Japanese *nana*) or the Sino-Japanese borrowing しち (from Middle Chinese *tshit* 'seven').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 七
Wiktionary — 七 (Japanese)

七号室.etymology: Sino-Japanese room-number compound 七号室 (ななごうしつ / しちごうしつ 'Room 7'), combining 七 ('seven') + 号 (ごう 'number, designation') + 室 (しつ 'room').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 号室
Wiktionary — 室 (Japanese)

七時.etymology: Clock-time compound 七時 (しちじ 'seven o'clock'), combining 七 (しち 'seven') + 時 (じ 'o'clock, hour').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 七時
Wiktionary — 七時 (しちじ) (Japanese)

七時半.etymology: Clock-time compound 七時半 (しちじはん 'half past seven, 7:30'), combining 七時 (しちじ 'seven o'clock') + 半 (はん 'half').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 七時
Wiktionary — 半 (Japanese)

七番.etymology: Numeral-classifier compound 七番 (ななばん / しちばん 'number seven, seventh'), combining 七 ('seven') + 番 (ばん 'numbered turn or position').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 七番
Wiktionary — 七番 (ななばん) (Japanese)

丈夫.etymology: Sino-Japanese adjectival noun 丈夫 (じょうぶ 'sturdy, durable, strong; in good health'). Wiktionary — テーブル (Japanese)

Wiktionary — 三分 (さんぷん) (Japanese)

三十.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound numeral 三十 (さんじゅう 'thirty'), combining 三 (さん 'three') + 十 (じゅう 'ten', alongside archaic native みそ *miso*).

全部.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adverb 全部 (ぜんぶ 'all, the whole, every part'), from 全 ('whole, entire') + 部 ('part, section, set of volumes'). Originally denoting 'a complete set of volumes of a book', in Meiji–Modern Japanese it generalized to 'all, everything'.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 再開 (Japanese)

写真.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 写 ('copy, depict') and 真 ('truth, the real thing'): 'copying the true likeness'. It first named painted portraits of deities and nobles; in the late Edo period it also meant drawing from life, and when photographs arrived from the West at the end of the Edo period it was adopted as the translation of English 'photograph', gradually replacing rivals such as 写真絵 and 照画.

几帳面.etymology: Adjectival noun 几帳面 (きちょうめん 'methodical, meticulous, neat and punctual'). Originally an architectural and woodworking term referring to the decorative chamfered grooves and rounded corners carved along the wooden posts of a Heian court screen-stand (几帳 *kichō*). Because the bevels were carved with unerring precision, in the Edo period 几帳面 came to describe a person who is scrupulously neat and exact.

堅苦しい.etymology: Native Japanese compound adjective formed from the stem of かたい (堅い・固い, 'hard, stiff, rigid') + くるしい (苦しい, 'painful, oppressive, stifling'), literally 'stiffly oppressive'.

history.form: 堅苦しい (かたくるしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 堅苦しい
Wiktionary — 堅苦しい (Japanese)

場所.etymology: Compound noun combining native Japanese ば (場, 'place, spot, arena') with the noun ところ/しょ (所, 'place, site'), read with the hybrid yomi ばしょ (jūbako reading).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 場所
Wiktionary — 場所 (Japanese)

塗り替える.etymology: Compound verb formed from the continuative stem ぬり (塗り, from 塗る 'to paint, coat, plaster') + かえる (替える, 'to replace, redo').

history.form: 塗り替える (ぬりかえる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗り替える
Wiktionary — 塗り替える (Japanese)

塗る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nuru* ('to smear, coat, plaster, paint'), attested in the Man'yōshū; likely related to ぬる (濡る, 'to get wet') and ぬるぬる ('slimy, slippery').

history.meaning: smear; daub; apply lacquer or mud

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗る
Wiktionary — 塗る (Japanese)

塩.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sifo* ('salt; seawater; tide'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, undergoing regular medial *-f- > -w- > Ø* change to modern *shio*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塩
Wiktionary — 塩 (Japanese)

塩バター.etymology: Modern hybrid culinary compound combining native Japanese しお (塩, 'salt') + loanword バター (from English *butter*), referring to salted butter or salt-butter flavoring.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — バター
Wiktionary — 塩 (Japanese)

壁.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kabe₁* ('mud or plaster wall, partition'), attested in the Man'yōshū and Wamyō Ruijushō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壁
Wiktionary — 壁 (Japanese)

壊す.etymology: Transitive godan verb *kowasu* ('to break, destroy, demolish'), formed as the transitive counterpart to こわれる (壊れる) from the verbal root *kowa-* ('break apart').

history.form: こぼつ / こわす (壊す)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壊す
Wiktionary — 壊す (Japanese)

壊れる.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *kowareru* ('to break, be broken, fall apart'), continuing Late Middle Japanese lower bigrade こわる (壊る), related to classical こぼつ/こぼる ('to break down').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壊れる
Wiktionary — 壊れる (Japanese)

声.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂we* ('voice, sound, cry'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-w-* was lost before *e* in Middle Japanese, yielding modern *koe*.

history.meaning: voice; vocal sound; cry of a bird or insect

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 声
Wiktionary — 声 (Japanese)

売る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uru* ('to sell, offer in exchange'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: sell; put on sale; make known (a name)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 売る
Wiktionary — 売る (Japanese)

売却.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 売却 (baikyaku), from 売 ('sell') + 却 (originally a completive particle in Chinese vernaculary usage, 'dispose of, away'), meaning 'selling off, disposal by sale'.

history.meaning: sell off; dispose of by sale

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 売却
Wiktionary — 売却 (Japanese)

壺.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tubo* ('round-bellied jar, pot, deep vessel'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Wamyō Ruijushō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壺
Wiktionary — 壺 (Japanese)

変.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and na-adjective 変 (hen), from Middle Chinese 變 (*pjiᴇnH*, 'change, transformation, unusual event, anomaly'); in Edo-period and modern Japanese used adjectivally for 'strange, odd, peculiar'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変
Wiktionary — 変 (Japanese)

変える.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *kaeru* ('to change, alter'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade かふ (変ふ・代ふ), the transitive partner of かわる (変わる).

history.meaning: exchange; alter; turn into something else

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変える
Wiktionary — 変える (Japanese)

変わる.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *kawaru* ('to change, be altered, vary'), continuing Old Japanese かはる (変はる・代はる), formed from the root *kafa-* + intransitive *-ru*.

history.meaning: undergo change; shift; take the place of
change; be transformed; vary; be unusual

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変わる
Wiktionary — 変わる (Japanese)

夏.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *natu* ('summer'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often compared internally with あつし (暑し・熱し, 'hot').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夏
Wiktionary — 夏 (Japanese)

夕方.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining ゆふ (夕, 'evening, dusk') + かた (方, 'direction, time around'), literally 'toward evening'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕方
Wiktionary — 夕方 (Japanese)

夕空.etymology: Native Japanese poetic and descriptive compound combining ゆう (夕, from Old Japanese *yufu*, 'evening') + そら (空, 'sky').

history.form: ゆふぞら / ゆふそら (夕空)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕空
Wiktionary — 夕空 (Japanese)

夕食.etymology: Compound of ゆう (夕, 'evening') + しょく (食, Sino-Japanese reading for 'meal, food'), or read purely Sino-Japanese as せきしょく; in modern standard usage read as the jūbako hybrid ゆうしょく ('evening meal, dinner').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕食
Wiktionary — 夕食 (Japanese)

外.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂to₂* ('outside, exterior, out of doors'), likely a compound of *so* ('back, away') + *to* ('place, door').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外
Wiktionary — 外 (Japanese)

外す.etymology: Transitive godan verb *hazusu* ('to unfasten, remove, miss'), paired with intransitive はずれる (外れる, classical はづる 'to come off, miss a notch').

history.meaning: release from the bowstring notch; undo; miss
unfasten; take off; remove; miss; step away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外す
Wiktionary — 外す (Japanese)

外側.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining そと (外, 'outside, exterior') + がわ (側, voiced from かわ 'side, row').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外側
Wiktionary — 外側 (Japanese)

多い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese adjective *oposi* (多し, 'numerous, abundant, many'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-p- > -f- > -w- > Ø* yielded modern *ōi*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 多い
Wiktionary — 多い (Japanese)

多め.etymology: Derived noun/na-adjective formed from the stem おお- of 多い ('many, much') + suffix -め (目, 'degree, tendency, somewhat on the ... side').

history.meaning: a generous amount; somewhat more than usual

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 多め
Wiktionary — 多め (Japanese)

夜.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yo₁ru* ('night'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, extended from the shorter root *yo₁* (夜, 'night') with the temporal/locative suffix *-ru* (compare *firu* 昼).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夜
Wiktionary — 夜 (Japanese)

夜分.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 夜分 (yabun), from 夜 ('night') + 分 ('division, time period'), attested in Chinese and adopted into Japanese as a polite expression for 'nighttime, late in the evening'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夜分
Wiktionary — 夜分 (Japanese)

夜明け.etymology: Native Japanese compound 夜明け (よあけ), from 夜 (よ, 'night') and 明け (あけ, nominalized stem of 明ける 'to grow light, dawn').
夜明け.notes: Evokes the transition from night darkness to first morning light.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 夜明け (Japanese)

夢.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yume₂* (earlier *ime₂*, 'dream'), attested in the Man'yōshū; widely analyzed as derived from い (寝, 'sleep') + め (目, 'eye, seeing'), literally 'sleep-vision'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夢
Wiktionary — 夢 (Japanese)

大きい.etymology: Adjectival derivative formed in Late Middle Japanese from Earlier Japanese おほきなり (大きなり, from Old Japanese *opoki₁* 'big, great'), shifting from a naru-adjective to an i-adjective.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大きい
Wiktionary — 大きい (Japanese)

大きな.etymology: Prenominal determiner (rentaishi) shortened from 大きなる (*ōkinaru*), the adnominal form of the classical naru-adjective 大きなり ('large, great').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大きな
Wiktionary — 大きな (Japanese)

大丈夫.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大丈夫 (daijōbu), originally from Classical Chinese ('a great, stalwart man of principle; a hero in full vigor'). In Japanese it shifted from 'strong, reliable person' to 'secure, sturdy, safe, all right'.

history.meaning: man of great stature and moral resolve
all right; safe; okay; no problem

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大丈夫
Wiktionary — 大丈夫 (Japanese)

大事.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大事 (daiji), from 大 ('great') + 事 ('matter, affair'). Originally 'a major event or grave crisis' in Buddhist and classical texts, whence 'something to be treated with great care, precious, important'.

history.meaning: great undertaking; matter of life and death
serious affair; emergency; something requiring care

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大事
Wiktionary — 大事 (Japanese)

大切.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大切 (taisetsu), from 大 ('great') + 切 ('urgent, pressing, keen'). Originally 'urgent necessity, critical moment' in medieval Japanese, later shifting to 'valuable, important, cherished'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大切
Wiktionary — 大切 (Japanese)

大声.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'big, loud') + ごえ (声, rendaku form of こえ 'voice').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大声
Wiktionary — 大声 (Japanese)

大変.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大変 (taihen), from 大 ('great, major') + 変 ('unusual event, calamity, upheaval'). From 'major disaster or serious incident', it bleached in Edo-period speech into 'dreadful, tough' and an intensifier 'very, extremely'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大変
Wiktionary — 大変 (Japanese)

大失敗.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound prefixing 大 (dai-, 'great, huge') to 失敗 (shippai, 'failure, blunder').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 失敗
Wiktionary — 失敗 (Japanese)

大好き.etymology: Hybrid compound prefixing Sino-Japanese 大 (dai-, 'greatly, very much') to native Japanese すき (好き, 'liking, fondness').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大好き
Wiktionary — 大好き (Japanese)

大家さん.etymology: Polite title formed from おおや (大家 / 大屋, 'main house; landlord, house-owner') + honorific suffix -さん (from さま 様).

history.meaning: landlord of a tenement or rental house

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大家
Wiktionary — 大家 (Japanese)

大工.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大工 (daiku), originally an official Ritsuryō court title ('master artisan, chief builder') above 小工 (shōku); by the medieval period it generalized to 'carpenter'.

history.meaning: chief master builder of state construction

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大工
Wiktionary — 大工 (Japanese)

大輝.etymology: Japanese masculine given name (commonly read Taiki or Daiki) composed of 大 ('great, large') + 輝 ('radiance, shine, brilliance').

history.form: 大輝 (たいき / だいき)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 輝
Wiktionary — 大輝 (Japanese)

大通り.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'large, main') + どおり (通り, rendaku form of とおり 'street, avenue, thoroughfare').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大通り
Wiktionary — 大通り (Japanese)

大阪.etymology: Major city and prefecture in the Kansai region; formerly written 大坂 ('great slope'), attested as 小坂 (Ozaka) in ancient texts and renamed 大坂 in the late 15th century, with the character 阪 standardized in the Meiji era.

history.form: 大坂 (おほさか / おおさか)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大阪
Wiktionary — 大阪 (Japanese)

大雨.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'heavy, great') + あめ (雨, 'rain'), attested since classical times.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大雨
Wiktionary — 大雨 (Japanese)

天井.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 天井 (tenjō), literally 'sky-well', referring originally in Chinese architecture and Japanese Buddhist temples to a coffered wooden lattice ceiling overhead, then any indoor ceiling.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 天井
Wiktionary — 天井 (Japanese)

天気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 天 ('sky, heavens') and 気 ('air, breath, atmospheric vapor'), meaning atmospheric weather.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 天気 (Japanese)

天気予報.etymology: Four-character Sino-Japanese compound 天気予報 (てんきよほう), pairing 天気 ('weather', literally 'sky energy') with 予報 ('advance report, forecast').
天気予報.notes: Coined in the Meiji meteorological service and used daily in broadcasts and conversation.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 天気予報 (Japanese)

太い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puto₁si* (太し, 'thick, stout, grand, sacredly auspicious'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: thick; fat; deep (of a voice); bold

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太い
Wiktionary — 太い (Japanese)

太っ腹.etymology: Colloquial compound formed from the geminated stem ふとっ- (from 太い 'thick, big') + はら (腹, 'belly, gut, spirit, disposition'), literally 'big-bellied' in the figurative sense of 'magnanimous, generous, big-hearted'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太っ腹
Wiktionary — 太っ腹 (Japanese)

太陽.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 太陽 (taiyō), from Classical Chinese 太陽 ('supreme yang; the sun', in contrast to 太陰 'supreme yin; the moon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太陽
Wiktionary — 太陽 (Japanese)

失くす.etymology: Transitive godan verb *nakusu* ('to lose, misplace, get rid of'), formed from the adverbial stem なく of ない (無い, 'nonexistent, gone') + transitive verbalizer -す (written with 失 by semantic association with 'losing').

history.meaning: cause to disappear; do away with; lose

history.form: 失くす / 無くす (なくす)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無くす
Wiktionary — 失くす (Japanese)

失礼.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 失礼 (shitsurei), from Classical Chinese 失禮 ('to fail in礼/etiquette, commit a breach of manners'); used in Japanese both for 'discourtesy, rudeness' and in polite apologies ('excuse me').

history.meaning: rudeness; breach of etiquette; excuse me

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 失礼
Wiktionary — 失礼 (Japanese)

契約.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 契約 (keiyaku), from Classical Chinese 契約 ('binding agreement, covenant'), combining 契 ('notched tally, deed, contract') + 約 ('bind, promise').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 契約
Wiktionary — 契約 (Japanese)

契約課.etymology: Sino-Japanese administrative compound combining 契約 (keiyaku, 'contract') + 課 (ka, 'administrative section, division, department').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 契約
Wiktionary — 契約 (Japanese)

奥.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂ku* ('interior, inner depths, far back'), attested in the Man'yōshū; contrasted with はし (端, 'edge') or おもて (表, 'front').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 奥
Wiktionary — 奥 (Japanese)

女性.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 女性 (josei), from 女 ('woman, female') + 性 ('sex, nature, gender'), used since classical times for the female sex and in modern Japanese as the standard polite noun for 'woman'.

history.form: 女性 (にょしょう / じょせい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 女性
Wiktionary — 女性 (Japanese)

好き.etymology: Nominal and na-adjectival form derived from the continuative stem of the Old Japanese verb すく (好く, 'to set one's heart on, be fond of, fancy').

history.meaning: fondness; devotion to poetry, love, or art

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 好き
Wiktionary — 好き (Japanese)

妙.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and na-adjective 妙 (myō), from Middle Chinese 妙 (*mjiewH*, 'wondrous, subtle, exquisite'). From Buddhist 'wondrous, beyond ordinary comprehension', it developed the colloquial sense 'strange, curious, peculiar'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 妙
Wiktionary — 妙 (Japanese)

始まり.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of はじまる (始まる, 'to begin, start').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始まり
Wiktionary — 始まり (Japanese)

始まる.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *hajimaru* ('to begin, start'), attested from Old Japanese, derived from the root of はじめ/はじむ (始む, 'to begin') + intransitive suffix *-aru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始まる
Wiktionary — 始まる (Japanese)

始める.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *hajimeru* ('to begin, start, initiate'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade はじむ (始む), cognate with はし (端, 'tip, first edge').

history.meaning: initiate; begin; do for the first time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始める
Wiktionary — 始める (Japanese)

姿.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sugata* ('bodily form, figure, appearance'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 姿
Wiktionary — 姿 (Japanese)

嬉しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uresi* (嬉し, 'joyful, delightful, pleasing'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; likely built on the emotional root *ura-* (裏・心, 'inner heart').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嬉しい
Wiktionary — 嬉しい (Japanese)

子.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₁* ('child, offspring, young, small thing'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子
Wiktionary — 子 (Japanese)

子ども.etymology: Orthographic variant of 子供 (*kodomo*, 'child, children'), formed from こ (子, 'child') + plural/collective suffix -ども (共, originally marking a group of subordinates or peers, later singularized).

history.form: 子ども / 子供 (こども)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子供
Wiktionary — 子ども (Japanese)

子供.etymology: Compound of Old Japanese こ (子, 'child') + plural suffix -ども (共). Originally plural ('children'), it reanalyzed in Early Modern Japanese as a singular or number-neutral noun for 'child' (pluralized again as 子供たち).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子供
Wiktionary — 子供 (Japanese)

字.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 字 (ji), from Middle Chinese 字 (*dziH*, 'written character, graph, courtesy name'), originally derived from 'to bear a child under a roof' > 'breed,衍生/derive characters'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 字
Wiktionary — 字 (Japanese)

学校.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 学校 (gakkō), from Classical Chinese 學校 ('school, place of learning'), combining 學 ('study, learn') + 校 ('school building, examine').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 学校
Wiktionary — 学校 (Japanese)

孫.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mago₁* (earlier *umago₁*, 'grandchild'), attested in the Wamyō Ruijushō; often analyzed as *uma-* + *ko₁* ('child').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 孫
Wiktionary — 孫 (Japanese)

守る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mamo₂ru* ('to watch closely, guard, protect'), attested in the Man'yōshū, derived from ま- (目, 'eye') + もる (守る, 'to guard, keep watch').

history.meaning: watch over with the eyes; guard; protect
protect; defend; obey (a rule); keep (a promise)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 守る
Wiktionary — 守る (Japanese)

安い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yasusi* (安し・易し, 'peaceful, calm, easy, free from anxiety'). In the Edo period, 'worry-free, easy to obtain' specialized when written 安い to 'inexpensive, cheap'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安い
Wiktionary — 安い (Japanese)

安全.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 安全 (anzen), from Classical Chinese 安全 ('safe and whole, free from danger'), combining 安 ('peaceful, secure') + 全 ('whole, intact').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安全
