床.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yuka* ('raised floor, platform, bed') and *to₂ko₂* ('sleeping platform, raised alcove, riverbed').

history.meaning: raised wooden floor or sleeping platform

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 床
Wiktionary — 床 (Japanese)

底.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂ko₂* ('bottom, lowest depth, far extremity'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 底
Wiktionary — 底 (Japanese)

店主さん.etymology: Polite form combining Sino-Japanese 店主 (tenshu, 'shopkeeper, store owner', from 店 'shop' + 主 'master, proprietor') + honorific suffix -さん.

history.form: 店主さん (てんしゅさん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店主
Wiktionary — 店主 (Japanese)

店内.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 店内 (tennai), combining 店 ('shop, store, restaurant') + 内 ('inside, interior').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店内
Wiktionary — 店内 (Japanese)

店員.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 店員 (ten'in), combining 店 ('shop, store') + 員 ('member, personnel, staff').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店員
Wiktionary — 店員 (Japanese)

座る.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *suwaru* (座る・据わる, 'to settle down in place, sit down'), the intransitive partner of すゑる/すえる (据える, 'to set in place'). Replaced classical ゐる (居る) as the everyday verb for 'to sit'.

history.meaning: be set firmly in place; sit down

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 座る
Wiktionary — 座る (Japanese)

座面.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 座面 (zamen), combining 座 ('seat, sitting') + 面 ('surface, face'), referring to the seating surface of a chair or stool.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 座面
Wiktionary — 座面 (Japanese)

庭.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nipa* ('flat open ground, courtyard for ceremonies or work, calm sea surface'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-p- > -w-* yielded modern *niwa*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 庭
Wiktionary — 庭 (Japanese)

庭用.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native Japanese にわ (庭, 'garden, yard') + Sino-Japanese suffix -よう (用, 'for the use of').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 庭
Wiktionary — 庭 (Japanese)

廊下.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 廊下 (rōka), from Chinese 廊下 ('under the roofed gallery/veranda'), combining 廊 ('covered corridor, colonnade') + 下 ('beneath').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 廊下
Wiktionary — 廊下 (Japanese)

建物.etymology: Native Japanese compound *tatemono* formed from the continuative stem たて of たてる (建てる, 'to erect, build') + もの (物, 'thing, structure').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建物
Wiktionary — 建物 (Japanese)

建築家.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 建築家 (kenchikuka), combining 建築 ('architecture, construction', from 建 'build' + 築 'construct') + specialist suffix -家 (-ka, 'expert, professional').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建築家
Wiktionary — 建築家 (Japanese)

建築規則.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound combining 建築 (kenchiku, 'building, architecture, construction') + 規則 (kisoku, 'regulation, rule, code').

history.form: 建築規則 (けんちくきそく)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建築
Wiktionary — 建築 (Japanese)

弁護士.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese legal coinage 弁護士 (bengoshi), officially adopted in the 1893 Attorney Act (弁護士法) to replace 代言人, combining 弁護 ('legal defense, advocacy') + professional suffix -士 ('qualified practitioner').

history.form: 辯護士 / 弁護士 (べんごし)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弁護士
Wiktionary — 弁護士 (Japanese)

式.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suffix 式 (shiki), from Middle Chinese 式 (*syik*, 'model, rule, ceremony, standard form, formula').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 式
Wiktionary — 式 (Japanese)

引き.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of ひく (引く, 'to pull, draw, subtract, patronize').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き
Wiktionary — 引き (Japanese)

引き上げる.etymology: Compound verb combining the continuative stem ひき (引き, 'pull, draw') + あげる (上げる, 'raise, lift up').

history.form: 引き上げる (ひきあげる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き上げる
Wiktionary — 引き上げる (Japanese)

引き出し.etymology: Nominalized continuative stem of the compound verb ひきだす (引き出す, 'to pull out, draw out'), lexicalized since the late medieval period for a sliding furniture drawer.

history.meaning: sliding box pulled out from a chest; withdrawal

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き出し
Wiktionary — 引き出し (Japanese)

引き出す.etymology: Compound verb combining the continuative stem ひき (引き, 'pull, draw') + だす (出す, 'take out, put forth').

history.form: ひきいだす / ひきだす (引き出す)

history.meaning: pull out; draw out; withdraw (money); elicit

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き出す
Wiktionary — 引き出す (Japanese)

引く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *piku* (引く・曳く, 'to pull, draw, tug, lead, play a stringed instrument'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: pull; draw; subtract; look up (in a dictionary); catch (a cold)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引く
Wiktionary — 引く (Japanese)

引っ越し業者.etymology: Compound noun combining ひっこし (引っ越し, 'moving house, relocation', from 引っ越す) + Sino-Japanese ぎょうしゃ (業者, 'business operator, contractor').

history.form: 引っ越し業者 (ひっこしぎょうしゃ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引越
Wiktionary — 引っ越し (Japanese)

弟.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂to₂-uto₂* (弟人, 'younger sibling/person'), a compound of *o₂to₂* ('younger, inferior in birth order', cognate with 劣る *otoru*) + *pito₂* (人, 'person') via sound change *-pito > -uto > -ōto*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弟
Wiktionary — 弟 (Japanese)

弟さん.etymology: Polite kinship noun formed from おとうと (弟, 'younger brother') + honorific suffix -さん, used to refer respectfully to someone else's younger brother.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弟
Wiktionary — 弟 (Japanese)

弦.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *turu* ('bowstring, taut cord') and also read Sino-Japanese *gen* (from Middle Chinese 弦 *ɣen*, 'bowstring, string of a musical instrument').

history.meaning: string (of a guitar, violin, or bow)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弦
Wiktionary — 弦 (Japanese)

張る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *paru* (張る, 'to stretch taut, spread, swell, bud'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: stretch tight (a bowstring or cloth); spread; bud
stretch; pitch (a tent); stick/paste; be expensive

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 張る
Wiktionary — 張る (Japanese)

強い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tuyosi* (強し, 'strong, mighty, firm, resilient'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 強い
Wiktionary — 強い (Japanese)

強がる.etymology: Derived godan verb formed from the stem つよ- of 強い ('strong') + verbal suffix -がる (marking outward display of a state or feeling, 'to act as if, put on a show of').

history.meaning: pretend to be tough; put on a brave front

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 強がる
Wiktionary — 強がる (Japanese)

弾く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *piku* ('to pluck or play a stringed instrument', etymologically identical to 引く 'to pull, draw across strings'), or read *hajiku* ('to flick, snap, repel').

history.meaning: pluck or stroke the strings of a koto or biwa
play (a stringed or keyboard instrument); flick

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弾く
Wiktionary — 弾く (Japanese)

当たり前.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun and na-adjective formed from あたり (当たり, 'allotted share, what corresponds') + まえ (前, 'portion, due share'), shifting in the Edo period from 'one's proper share' to 'natural, only to be expected, obvious'.

history.form: あたりまへ (当前・当たり前)
history.meaning: one's due portion; what is proper and natural

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当たり前
Wiktionary — 当たり前 (Japanese)

当たる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *ataru* ('to hit, strike against, face, correspond to'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: hit; be exposed to (sun/wind); succeed; be right

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当たる
Wiktionary — 当たる (Japanese)

当てる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *ateru* ('to hit, apply, expose to, guess'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade あつ (当つ・充つ), the transitive partner of あたる (当たる).

history.meaning: apply to; press against; assign; hit

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当てる
Wiktionary — 当てる (Japanese)

当館.etymology: Sino-Japanese formal compound 当館 (tōkan), combining proximal/reflexive prefix 当 ('this, our') + 館 ('hall, inn, museum, building').

history.meaning: this inn/hotel; this museum/library; our establishment

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当館
Wiktionary — 当館 (Japanese)

彫る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *poru* (彫る・掘る, 'to dig out, hollow out, carve, engrave'); originally a single verb written 掘る for digging earth and 彫る for carving wood, stone, or metal.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彫る
Wiktionary — 彫る (Japanese)

影.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kage₂* ('light, reflection, visual image, silhouette, shade/shadow'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; originally denoted both gleaming light/reflection and the dark shadow cast by an object.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 影
Wiktionary — 影 (Japanese)

役.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 役 (yaku / eki), from Middle Chinese 役 (*jwek*, 'corvée labor, military service, official duty'); in Japanese extended to 'assigned office, role, dramatic part, usefulness'.

history.meaning: role; part (in a play); position; service/use

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 役
Wiktionary — 役 (Japanese)

役所.etymology: Compound combining Sino-Japanese やく (役, 'public office, official duty') + しょ (所, 'place, office'), attested from medieval Japanese for a post of official duty or government office.

history.meaning: post of official duty; magistrate's or government office
government office; public office; municipal hall

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 役所
Wiktionary — 役所 (Japanese)

彼.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese distal demonstrative *kare* (彼, 'that thing or person over there', formed from distal root *ka-* + suffix *-re*). Under Western translation influence in the Meiji era, it specialized as the third-person masculine pronoun 'he' (and 'boyfriend').

history.meaning: that one over there; that person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彼
Wiktionary — 彼 (Japanese)

彼ら.etymology: Third-person plural pronoun formed from 彼 (kare, 'that person; he') + pluralizing suffix -ら (等, from Old Japanese *-ra*). Attested since classical times for 'those people' and used in modern Japanese for 'they, them'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彼ら
Wiktionary — 彼ら (Japanese)

往復.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 往復 (ōfuku), from Classical Chinese 往復 ('going and returning'), combining 往 ('go') + 復 ('return').

history.meaning: round trip; going and returning; correspondence

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 往復
Wiktionary — 往復 (Japanese)

待つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *matu* (待つ, 'to wait for, await, expect'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 待つ
Wiktionary — 待つ (Japanese)

後.etymology: Read both as *ato* (from Old Japanese *ato* 'footprint, track, behind, after') and *nochi* (from Old Japanese *no₂ti* 'later time, future, posterity'), as well as Sino-Japanese *go / kō*.

history.form: 後 (あと / のち / ご)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後
Wiktionary — 後 (Japanese)

後ろ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *usiro₁* (後ろ, 'back side, space behind, rear'), formed from the root *usi-* (possibly related to *ura* 'back') + locative noun suffix *-ro₁*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後ろ
Wiktionary — 後ろ (Japanese)

後半.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 後半 (kōhan), combining 後 ('latter, behind, after') + 半 ('half'), meaning 'the second half, latter half'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後半
Wiktionary — 後半 (Japanese)

心臓.etymology: Sino-Japanese anatomical compound 心臓 (shinzō), from traditional Chinese medicine 五臓 (the five viscera), combining 心 ('heart') + 臓 ('internal organ, viscus').

history.meaning: the heart organ among the five viscera

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 心臓
Wiktionary — 心臓 (Japanese)

心配.etymology: Japanese-coined or Early Modern Sino-Japanese compound 心配 (shinpai), combining 心 ('mind, heart') + 配 ('distribute, deploy, pay attention to' — compare native 気を配る 'to pay attention, be on guard').

history.meaning: putting one's mind to every detail; anxiety; care

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 心配
Wiktionary — 心配 (Japanese)

必ず.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese adverb *kanarazu* (必ず, 'without fail, certainly, necessarily'), lexicalized from the negative form *kanarazu* of a defective verb *kanaru* ('to be tentative/partial' or related to 兼ねる 'to hold two possibilities').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 必ず
Wiktionary — 必ず (Japanese)

必要.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 必要 (hitsuyō), from Classical/Tang Chinese 必要 ('indispensable, must-have'), combining 必 ('certainly, inevitably') + 要 ('essential, need').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 必要
Wiktionary — 必要 (Japanese)

忘れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *wasuru* (忘る, 'to let slip from the mind, forget'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *wasureru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 忘れる
Wiktionary — 忘れる (Japanese)

忘れ物センター.etymology: Modern hybrid compound combining わすれもの (忘れ物, 'lost article, item left behind', from 忘れる + 物) + loanword センター (from English *center*).

history.form: 忘れ物センター (わすれものセンター)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 忘れ物
Wiktionary — 忘れ物 (Japanese)

快適.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 快適 (kaiteki), from Chinese 快適 ('pleasant and agreeable'), combining 快 ('pleasant, refreshing') + 適 ('fit, comfortable, agreeable').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 快適
Wiktionary — 快適 (Japanese)

怒る.etymology: Read both as *okoru* (originally 興る・起こる 'to rise up, flare up' of temper, applied to 怒る in Early Modern Japanese) and *ikaru* (inherited from Old Japanese *ikaru* 'to bristle with rage, become furious').

history.meaning: lose one's temper; get angry; scold

history.form: 怒る (おこる / いかる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怒る
Wiktionary — 怒る (Japanese)

怒鳴る.etymology: Early Modern Japanese compound verb *donaru* ('to shout, bellow, yell angrily'), formed from a reinforced prefix ど- (度 / 怒) + なる (鳴る, 'to sound, roar, ring out'), later spelled ateji-style with 怒 ('anger').

history.form: どなる (度鳴る・怒鳴る)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怒鳴る
Wiktionary — 怒鳴る (Japanese)

怖い.etymology: Shifted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from classical こはし (強し・剛し, 'hard, stiff, unyielding, intimidating') to 'frightening, scary, fearful'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怖い
Wiktionary — 怖い (Japanese)

思い出.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from the continuative stem おもひで of the classical verb おもひいづ / おもひづ (思ひ出づ, 'to come to mind, recall, recollect').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思い出
Wiktionary — 思い出 (Japanese)

思い出す.etymology: Compound godan verb combining the continuative stem おもい (思い, 'think, feel') + だす (出す, 'bring out, call forth'), replacing earlier lower bigrade 思ひ出づ.

history.form: おもひいだす / おもひだす (思ひ出す)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思い出す
Wiktionary — 思い出す (Japanese)

思う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂mo₂pu* (思ふ, 'to think, feel in one's heart, love, yearn for'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often connected with おも (面, 'face, expression').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思う
Wiktionary — 思う (Japanese)

急ぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *iso₁gu* (急ぐ, 'to prepare busily, hasten, hurry'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急ぐ
Wiktionary — 急ぐ (Japanese)

急便.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 急便 (kyūbin), combining 急 ('urgent, rapid, express') + 便 ('dispatch, mail/courier service').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急便
Wiktionary — 急便 (Japanese)

急須.etymology: Borrowed from early modern southern Chinese (Min / Wu pronunciation of 急須 or 急焼, a small vessel for quickly warming wine or steeping tea), adopted in Edo-period sencha culture for a small side-handled teapot.

history.meaning: small quick-heating pot for wine or tea

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急須
Wiktionary — 急須 (Japanese)

恥ずかしい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *padukasi* (恥づかし, 'admirable to the point of making one feel inadequate; bashful; ashamed'), derived from the verb はづ (恥づ, modern 恥じる 'to feel shame').

history.meaning: so impressive as to humble the observer; bashful; shameful

history.form: 恥ずかしい (はずかしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 恥ずかしい
Wiktionary — 恥ずかしい (Japanese)

息.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *oki₁* > *iki₁* ('breath, respiration, vital spirit'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with いく (生く, 'to live').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 息
Wiktionary — 息 (Japanese)

息切れ.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining いき (息, 'breath') + ぎれ (切れ, rendaku form of きれ from 切れる 'to run out, be cut off').

history.meaning: shortness of breath; panting; running out of steam

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 息切れ
Wiktionary — 息切れ (Japanese)

悩み.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of なやむ (悩む, Old Japanese *nayamu* 'to suffer illness, ache, be troubled or distressed').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 悩み
Wiktionary — 悩み (Japanese)

悪い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *warusi* (悪し, 'inferior, poor in quality, undesirable, bad'), attested in the Man'yōshū; gradually took over the semantic territory of classical あし (悪し).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 悪い
Wiktionary — 悪い (Japanese)

意味.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 意味 (imi), from Classical and Buddhist Chinese 意味 ('thought and flavor; underlying significance, purport, meaning').

history.meaning: import and flavor of words; meaning

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 意味
Wiktionary — 意味 (Japanese)

意地.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 意地 (iji), originally a Buddhist term translating Sanskrit *manobhūmi* ('the ground/plane of mind and thought'); in Early Modern Japanese it shifted to 'disposition, stubborn pride, willpower'.

history.meaning: stubbornness; pride; willpower; appetite (in 意地が汚い)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 意地
Wiktionary — 意地 (Japanese)

感じ.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from the continuative stem of the Sino-Japanese suru/zuru-verb 感ず / 感じる (from Middle Chinese 感 'to be moved, feel, sense').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 感じ
Wiktionary — 感じ (Japanese)

感傷.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 感傷 (kanshō), from Classical Chinese 感傷 ('to be moved to sorrow, feel sentimental grief'), combining 感 ('be moved, feel') + 傷 ('wound, grieve').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 感傷
Wiktionary — 感傷 (Japanese)

慌てる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *awatu* (慌つ, 'to be flustered, lose one's composure, panic'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: be flustered; be thrown into confusion
hurry in confusion; panic; be flustered

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 慌てる
Wiktionary — 慌てる (Japanese)

気.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 気 (ki / ke), from Middle Chinese 氣 (*kʰjɨjH*, 'vapor, breath, vital energy, spirit, mood, disposition'), deeply integrated into Japanese idiom for mind, attention, and atmosphere.

history.meaning: spirit; mind; heart; mood; attention; air/sign

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気
Wiktionary — 気 (Japanese)

気づく.etymology: Compound godan verb *kizuku* (気づく・気付く), grammaticalized from the clause 気がつく ('one's attention/mind attaches to something -> to notice, realize, regain consciousness').

history.form: きがつく / きづく (気付く)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気付く
Wiktionary — 気づく (Japanese)

気に入る.etymology: Idiomatic phrasal verb 気に入る (ki ni iru, 'to enter into one's spirit/fancy'), attested from late medieval and Edo Japanese for 'to be pleased with, like, take a liking to'.

history.meaning: suit one's mind or taste; be pleasing
like; be pleased with; take a fancy to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気に入る
Wiktionary — 気に入る (Japanese)

気の毒.etymology: Nominal/na-adjectival phrase 気の毒 (ki no doku), literally 'poison to the spirit'. In Edo-period usage it first meant 'troublesome or regrettable to one's own mind', and subsequently shifted to 'pitiful, unfortunate, feeling sorry for someone else'.

history.meaning: pitiful; unfortunate; sorry to trouble you

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気の毒
Wiktionary — 気の毒 (Japanese)

気分.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 気分 (kibun), combining 気 ('vital spirit, mood, humor') + 分 ('state, condition, lot'), denoting one's physical or emotional mood and state of feeling.

history.meaning: state of health or humor; mood
feeling; mood; state of health; atmosphere

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気分
Wiktionary — 気分 (Japanese)

気持ち.etymology: Hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese き (気, 'mind, spirit, mood') + native Japanese もち (持ち, from 持つ 'holding, maintaining').

history.meaning: way of holding one's mind; frame of mind; sensation

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気持ち
Wiktionary — 気持ち (Japanese)

気持ちよい.etymology: Compound adjective combining きもち (気持ち, 'feeling, sensation') + よい (良い, 'good, pleasant'), meaning 'pleasant, comfortable, refreshing'.

history.form: 気持ちよい / 気持ち良い (きもちよい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気持ち良い
Wiktionary — 気持ちいい (Japanese)

気軽.etymology: Hybrid na-adjective combining Sino-Japanese き (気, 'spirit, mind, mood') + native Japanese がる (軽, rendaku form of the stem かる- of 軽い 'light').

history.meaning: lighthearted; casual; free and easy; unhesitating

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気軽
Wiktionary — 気軽 (Japanese)

水.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mi₁du* (水, combining form *mi₁-*, 'water, fresh cold water'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *sui* (from Middle Chinese 水 *sywijX*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水
Wiktionary — 水 (Japanese)

水性.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水性 (suisei), combining 水 ('water') + 性 ('nature, property'), referring in modern usage especially to water-based paints, inks, or adhesives.

history.meaning: the nature of water; aquatic nature

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水性
Wiktionary — 水性 (Japanese)

水曜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水曜 (suiyō), literally 'luminary of Mercury (the Water Star, 水星)' from the classical seven-planet astrological cycle, serving as the short form of 水曜日 ('Wednesday').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水曜
Wiktionary — 水曜 (Japanese)

水曜日.etymology: Compound of 水曜 ('Mercury day', linked to the Five Phases element 水 'water') and 日 ('day') in the seven-day week.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 水曜日 (Japanese)

水漏れ.etymology: Hybrid/native compound combining みず (水, 'water') + もれ (漏れ, continuative stem of 漏れる 'to leak').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水漏れ
Wiktionary — 水漏れ (Japanese)

水道管.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水道管 (suidōkan), combining 水道 ('waterworks, water supply conduit', from 水 'water' + 道 'channel/way') + 管 ('pipe, tube').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水道管
Wiktionary — 水道管 (Japanese)

氷.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂pori* (氷, 'ice'), nominalized from the continuative stem of the Old Japanese verb *ko₂poru* (氷る・凍る, 'to freeze, congeal'); underwent medial *-p- > -f- > -w- > Ø* to modern *kōri*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 氷
Wiktionary — 氷 (Japanese)

決定.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 決定 (kettei), from Classical and Buddhist Chinese 決定 ('to settle decisively, fix without doubt'), combining 決 ('breach a dike, decide, resolve') + 定 ('fix, settle').

history.form: けつぢゃう / けってい (決定)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 決定
Wiktionary — 決定 (Japanese)

汽車.etymology: Late Edo / Meiji-era Sino-Japanese compound 汽車 (kisha), combining 汽 ('steam, vapor', short for 蒸気 *jōki*) + 車 ('wheeled vehicle, carriage'), coined for a steam train.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 汽車
Wiktionary — 汽車 (Japanese)

油.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *abura* (油・脂, 'oil, fat, grease, tallow'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 油
Wiktionary — 油 (Japanese)

油断.etymology: Sino-Japanese / Buddhist compound 油断 (yudan), literally 'cutting off the flow of oil'. Derived from a parable in the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (涅槃経) in which a man ordered to carry a bowl brimful of oil without spilling a single drop on pain of death must never relax his attention; hence 'momentary lapse of attention, carelessness, negligence'.

history.meaning: letting one's guard or attention lapse
negligence; carelessness; inattention; being off one's guard

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 油断
Wiktionary — 油断 (Japanese)

沿う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *so₂pu* (添ふ・沿ふ, 'to accompany closely, run alongside, conform to'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; spelled 沿う specifically when following a line, river, road, or policy.

history.meaning: run along; follow (a river, road, or plan); meet (expectations)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 沿う
Wiktionary — 沿う (Japanese)

泊まる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *to₂maru* (泊まる・止まる・留まる, 'to stop, come to rest, anchor in a harbor, stay overnight'), specialized in orthography as 泊まる for anchoring a boat or lodging for the night.

history.meaning: moor a boat for the night; lodge overnight

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泊まる
Wiktionary — 泊まる (Japanese)

法律.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 法律 (hōritsu), from Classical Chinese 法律 ('laws and statutes'), combining 法 ('law, norm, model') + 律 ('penal statute, code'); adopted in the Meiji era as the standard term for statutory law.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 法律
Wiktionary — 法律 (Japanese)

泡.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *awa* (泡・沫, 'foam, bubble, froth on water'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泡
Wiktionary — 泡 (Japanese)

泡立てる.etymology: Compound ichidan verb combining あわ (泡, 'foam, bubbles') + たてる (立てる, 'to raise, whip up').

history.form: あわだつ / あわだてる (泡立てる)
history.meaning: work into a foam; whip up lather

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泡立てる
Wiktionary — 泡立てる (Japanese)

泣く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *naku* (泣く・鳴く, 'to cry out, weep, sing/call of birds and animals'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; written 泣く for human weeping and 鳴く for animal/bird cries.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泣く
Wiktionary — 泣く (Japanese)

注ぎ口.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining そそぎ (注ぎ, continuative stem of 注ぐ 'to pour') + ぐち (口, rendaku form of くち 'mouth, opening, spout').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 注ぎ口
Wiktionary — 注ぎ口 (Japanese)

注ぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂so₂ku* > *sosogu* (注ぐ・灌ぐ, 'to pour liquid into, flow into, sprinkle, devote oneself to') and *tsugu* (注ぐ・継ぐ, 'to pour into a cup or vessel').

history.form: そそく / そそぐ (注ぐ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 注ぐ
Wiktionary — 注ぐ (Japanese)

注文.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 注 ('pour, fix attention, annotate') and 文 ('writing, document'), which shifted in medieval/early-modern Japanese commerce from 'an itemized written list' to 'placing an order for goods'.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 注文 (Japanese)

洋風.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 洋風 (yōfū), combining 洋 ('Western, overseas', short for 西洋 *seiyō*) + 風 ('style, manner'), contrasted with 和風 (wafū, 'Japanese style').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洋風
Wiktionary — 洋風 (Japanese)

洗う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *arapu* (洗ふ, 'to wash with water, cleanse, rinse, investigate'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洗う
Wiktionary — 洗う (Japanese)

洗面所.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 洗面所 (senmenjo), combining 洗面 ('washing the face', from 洗 'wash' + 面 'face') + 所 ('place, room').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洗面所
Wiktionary — 洗面所 (Japanese)

流す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *nagasu* (流す, 'to let flow, set adrift, wash away, exile'), paired with intransitive ながる/ながれる (流れる).

history.meaning: set afloat on a current; wash away; banish
let flow; drain; flush; broadcast/play (music); shed (tears/sweat)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 流す
Wiktionary — 流す (Japanese)

流れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *nagaru* (流る, 'to flow, stream, drift along, pass by'), becoming modern ichidan *nagareru*.

history.meaning: flow; stream; drift; be washed away; be called off

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 流れる
Wiktionary — 流れる (Japanese)

海塩.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 海塩 (かいえん), from 海 ('sea, ocean') and 塩 ('salt').
海塩.notes: Distinguishes evaporated sea salt from rock salt (岩塩 がんえん).

sources.title: Wiktionary — 海塩 (Japanese)

浸す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *pitasu* (浸す・漬す, 'to soak, steep, dip in liquid'), paired with intransitive ひたる (浸る, 'to be immersed in').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 浸す
Wiktionary — 浸す (Japanese)

消える.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *ki₁yu* (消ゆ, 'to melt away, go out, vanish, disappear'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *kieru*.

history.meaning: melt (of snow/dew); go out (of fire); vanish
go out; disappear; vanish; fade away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 消える
Wiktionary — 消える (Japanese)

深い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pukasi* (深し, 'deep, profound, dense, late in a season or night'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: deep; profound; thick (of fog/woods); close (of a relationship)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 深い
Wiktionary — 深い (Japanese)

深呼吸.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 深呼吸 (shinkokyū), prefixing 深 ('deep') to 呼吸 ('breathing, respiration', from 呼 'exhale' + 吸 'inhale').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 深呼吸
Wiktionary — 深呼吸 (Japanese)

混ぜる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *mazeru* ('to mix, blend, stir together'), continuing Classical Japanese lower bigrade まず (混ず・交ず), paired with intransitive まじる/まざる (混じる・混ざる).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 混ぜる
Wiktionary — 混ぜる (Japanese)

混む.etymology: Inherited from Classical and Late Middle Japanese *komu* (込む・混む, 'to crowd in, be packed together'), specialized in modern orthography as 混む when referring to crowds or traffic congestion.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 混む
Wiktionary — 混む (Japanese)

清潔.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 清潔 (seiketsu), from Classical Chinese 清潔 ('clear and pure, uncorrupted, clean'), combining 清 ('clear, pure') + 潔 ('clean, spotless').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 清潔
Wiktionary — 清潔 (Japanese)

済ませる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *sumaseru* ('to finish, get through with, settle, make do with'), originally the causative form of すむ (済む, 'to come to an end, be settled'), alongside godan 済ます.

history.form: すませる / すます (済ませる)
history.meaning: bring to completion; settle; make do
finish; get done; settle; make do with

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 済ませる
Wiktionary — 済ませる (Japanese)

済む.etymology: Etymologically the same native Japanese verb as すむ (澄む, 'to become clear, settle' of muddy water). In Early Modern merchant and everyday usage, 'for things to settle down without trouble' developed the sense 'to be settled (of an account or business), be finished, be over', written with 済.

history.meaning: be settled (of debts or affairs); come to a close
end; be completed; be settled; be excusable

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 済む
Wiktionary — 済む (Japanese)

渡す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *watasu* (渡す, 'to carry across water, bridge across, hand over'), paired with intransitive わたる (渡る).

history.meaning: ferry across; span across; hand over
hand over; deliver; ferry across; lay across

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡す
Wiktionary — 渡す (Japanese)

渡せる.etymology: Potential ichidan form (*wataseru*, 'can hand over, be able to pass/deliver') derived from the godan verb わたす (渡す, 'to hand over, pass across').

history.meaning: be able to hand over; can give/deliver

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡す
Wiktionary — 渡せる (Japanese)

渡る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *wataru* (渡る・亘る, 'to cross over water or a bridge, pass across, extend throughout'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: cross over (a river, sea, or sky); pass through
cross (a bridge, street, or river); migrate; be handed over

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡る
Wiktionary — 渡る (Japanese)

温かい.etymology: Same native Japanese word *atatakai* as 暖かい (from classical あたたかなり 'warm, mild'), conventionally written 温かい when referring to warm food, liquids, touch, or human kindness.

history.form: あたたかなり (温かなり)

history.meaning: warm (to the touch, of food/drink, or of heart/reception)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 温かい
Wiktionary — 温かい (Japanese)

測る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pakaru* (測る・量る・計る・図る, 'to reckon, measure, weigh, fathom, plan'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; spelled 測る specifically for measuring depth, length, area, or physical quantities.

history.form: はかる (測る・量る・計る)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 測る
Wiktionary — 測る (Japanese)

湯呑み.etymology: Native Japanese compound 湯呑み / 湯飲み (yunomi), from ゆ (湯, 'hot water, hot tea') + のみ (飲み, continuative stem of 飲む 'to drink'), referring to a cylindrical handleless ceramic teacup.

history.form: ゆのみ (湯飲み・湯呑み)
history.meaning: cup for drinking hot water or tea

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 湯呑み
Wiktionary — 湯呑み (Japanese)

湿る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sime₂ru* (湿る, 'to become damp, moisten, be subdued or quiet'), attested in the Man'yōshū; paired with transitive しめす (湿す).

history.meaning: absorb moisture; become damp; grow quiet
become damp; get moist; be dampened

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 湿る
Wiktionary — 湿る (Japanese)

湿気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 湿気 (colloquially read しっけ with gemination, alongside しっき), from 湿 ('damp, moist') and 気 ('air, vapour').
湿気.notes: Central everyday word during Japan's rainy season when wooden doors and piano actions absorb moisture.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 湿気 (Japanese)

満室.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満室 (manshitsu), combining 満 ('full') + 室 ('room'), indicating that a hotel, inn, or building has no vacancies.

history.meaning: no vacancy; fully booked (of rooms); full room

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満室
Wiktionary — 満室 (Japanese)

満杯.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満杯 (manpai), combining 満 ('full') + 杯 ('cup, vessel, capacity'), literally 'a full cup' and by extension 'filled to capacity, chock-full'.

history.meaning: a cup filled to the brim

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満杯
Wiktionary — 満杯 (Japanese)

満点.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満点 (manten), combining 満 ('full, complete') + 点 ('point, mark, score'), meaning a perfect score or full marks.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満点
Wiktionary — 満点 (Japanese)

準備.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 準備 (junbi), from Chinese 準備 ('to prepare beforehand, make ready in advance'), combining 準 ('level, standard, prepare') + 備 ('provide, equip, get ready').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 準備
Wiktionary — 準備 (Japanese)

滑る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sube₂ru* (滑る・辷る, 'to slide smoothly, slip, glide'), attested in the Kojiki and Wamyō Ruijushō; cognate with すべすべ ('smooth').

history.meaning: glide; slip smoothly; step down from the throne
slip; slide; glide; skate/ski; fall flat (of a joke)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 滑る
Wiktionary — 滑る (Japanese)

澄む.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sumu* (澄む・清む, 'to become clear, transparent, untroubled, or pure' of water, sky, sound, or mind), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: become clear and limpid (of water, moon, or sound)
become clear; be transparent; be serene

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 澄む
Wiktionary — 澄む (Japanese)

激しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pagesi* (激し・烈し, 'fierce, violent, tempestuous, intense'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: fierce (of wind or current); violent; intense

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 激しい
Wiktionary — 激しい (Japanese)

濃い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂si* (濃し, 'deep in color, thick in consistency, strong in flavor'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濃い
Wiktionary — 濃い (Japanese)

濡らす.etymology: Transitive godan verb *nurasu* ('to wet, moisten, drench'), paired with intransitive ぬる/ぬれる (濡れる).

history.meaning: make wet; dampen with water, dew, or tears

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濡らす
Wiktionary — 濡らす (Japanese)

濡れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *nuru* (濡る, 'to get wet, become damp'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *nureru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濡れる
Wiktionary — 濡れる (Japanese)

火.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pi₂* (combining form *po₂-*, 'fire, flame'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *ka* (from Middle Chinese 火 *xwaX*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 火
Wiktionary — 火 (Japanese)

火曜日.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 火曜日 (kayōbi), combining 火曜 ('Day of Mars, the Fire Star 火星' in the classical seven-luminary astrological cycle) + 日 ('day').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 火曜日
Wiktionary — 火曜日 (Japanese)

灰色.etymology: Compound combining native Japanese はい (灰, from Old Japanese *papi* 'ash') + いろ (色, 'color'), literally 'ash color'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 灰色
Wiktionary — 灰色 (Japanese)

炎.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *po₂-no-po* (火の穂, literally 'ear/spike of fire', comparing a leaping tongue of flame to an ear of grain *po*), which contracted via *ponopo > fonofo > honoo*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 炎
Wiktionary — 炎 (Japanese)

炭酸水.etymology: Modern Sino-Japanese scientific and culinary compound 炭酸水 (tansansui), combining 炭酸 ('carbonic acid, carbonation', coined in the late Edo/Rangaku period from 炭 'carbon' + 酸 'acid') + 水 ('water').

history.meaning: carbonated water; sparkling water; soda water

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 炭酸水
Wiktionary — 炭酸水 (Japanese)

点.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 点 (ten), from Middle Chinese 點 (*temX*, 'small black fleck, dot, speck, mark, point, to light/drip').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 点
Wiktionary — 点 (Japanese)

点数.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 点数 (tensū), combining 点 ('point, mark, item') + 数 ('number, count'), denoting either a numerical score/grade or the number of items.

history.meaning: count of items; number of points
score; points; marks; number of items

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 点数
Wiktionary — 点数 (Japanese)

無事.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無事 (buji), from Classical Chinese 無事 ('without incident, free from trouble or warfare, at peace'), combining 無 ('without') + 事 ('untoward incident, affair').

history.meaning: free of trouble or military incident; peaceful
safe; without incident; safe and sound

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無事
Wiktionary — 無事 (Japanese)

無塗装.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無塗装 (mutosō), prefixing privative 無 ('un-, without') to 塗装 ('painting, coating, finish', from 塗 'paint/coat' + 装 'finish/dress').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗装
Wiktionary — 塗装 (Japanese)

無塩バター.etymology: Modern culinary compound combining Sino-Japanese 無塩 (muen, 'unsalted, salt-free', from 無 'without' + 塩 'salt') + loanword バター (from English *butter*).

history.form: 無塩バター (むえんバター)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — バター
Wiktionary — バター (Japanese)

無料.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無料 (muryō), combining privative 無 ('without, no') + 料 ('fee, charge, material').

history.meaning: free of charge; complimentary; no fee

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無料
Wiktionary — 無料 (Japanese)

無理.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無理 (muri), from Classical and Song Neo-Confucian Chinese 無理 ('contrary to reason or principle'), combining 無 ('without') + 理 ('reason, natural order'). Extended in Japanese to 'unreasonable, forced, impossible, overdoing it'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無理
Wiktionary — 無理 (Japanese)

焼き.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of やく (焼く, 'to burn, roast, grill, bake, fire pottery').

history.meaning: roasting; grilling; firing of pottery or blades
cooking on heat; grilling; baking; ceramic ware

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 焼き
Wiktionary — 焼き (Japanese)

焼きたて.etymology: Compound formed from the continuative stem やき (焼き, from 焼く 'to bake, grill, roast') + suffix -たて (立て, 'just finished doing, freshly ...').

history.form: 焼きたて / 焼き立て (やきたて)
history.meaning: freshly baked; freshly grilled; hot from the oven

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 焼き立て
Wiktionary — 焼きたて (Japanese)

焼く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *yaku* (焼く, 'to burn, set on fire, roast, bake, fire clay, char'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: bake; grill; roast; toast; burn; tan

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 焼く
Wiktionary — 焼く (Japanese)

焼ける.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *yakeru* ('to burn, be baked, be roasted, be sunburned, glow red at sunset'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade やく (焼く), the intransitive partner of godan 焼く.

history.meaning: burn; be consumed by fire; be roasted
be baked/grilled; burn down; get sunburned; glow (of sunset)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 焼ける
Wiktionary — 焼ける (Japanese)

照らす.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *terasu* (照らす, 'to shine upon, illuminate, compare against'), derived from intransitive てる (照る, 'to shine') + transitive suffix *-asu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 照らす
Wiktionary — 照らす (Japanese)

熱.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 熱 (netsu), from Middle Chinese 熱 (*nyet*, 'heat, high temperature, fever, ardor').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 熱
Wiktionary — 熱 (Japanese)

熱々.etymology: Reduplicated native Japanese nominal/na-adjectival expression 熱々 (atsuatsu), reduplicating the stem あつ- of 熱い ('hot'), used for piping-hot food or a passionately lovestruck couple.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 熱々
Wiktionary — 熱々 (Japanese)

熱い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *atusi* (熱し・暑し, 'hot to the touch, hot of weather, fervent'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; spelled 熱い for objects, liquids, and emotion (and 暑い for ambient weather).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 熱い
Wiktionary — 熱い (Japanese)

片付ける.etymology: Compound ichidan verb *katazukeru* (片付ける, 'to put in order, tidy up, clear away, finish off, marry off'), transitive partner of かたづく (片付く, literally 'to settle to one side [片]').

history.meaning: put away neatly to one side; settle; dispose of
tidy up; put in order; clear away; finish

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 片付ける
Wiktionary — 片付ける (Japanese)

牛乳.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 牛 ('cow, cattle') and 乳 ('milk'), literally 'cow's milk'.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 牛乳 (Japanese)

物.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mo₂no₂* (物, 'thing, tangible object, being, spirit, matter'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *butsu / motsu* (from Middle Chinese 物 *mjut*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 物
Wiktionary — 物 (Japanese)

物件売却.etymology: Sino-Japanese real-estate and legal compound combining 物件 (bukken, 'property, real-estate object, article') + 売却 (baikyaku, 'sale, disposal by sale').

history.form: 物件売却 (ぶっけんばいきゃく)
history.meaning: property sale; sale of real estate

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 売却
Wiktionary — 売却 (Japanese)

特別.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 特別 (tokubetsu), combining 特 ('special, singled out, exceptional') + 別 ('separate, distinct, different').

history.stage: Late Imperial Chinese / Early Modern Japanese

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 特別
Wiktionary — 特別 (Japanese)

狂い.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of くるう (狂う, Old Japanese *kurupu* 'to go mad, get out of order, warp, go awry').

history.meaning: madness; frenzy; deviation from true alignment
warping (of wood); going out of order; discrepancy; madness

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 狂い
Wiktionary — 狂い (Japanese)

狭い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *se₂basi* / *se₂masi* (狭し, 'narrow, cramped, small in area'), built on the spatial root *se-* (狭, 'narrow place, rapids', as in 瀬戸 *seto*). Medial *-b-* and *-m-* alternated in Middle Japanese, yielding standard *semai*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 狭い
Wiktionary — 狭い (Japanese)

猶予.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 猶予 (yūyo), from Classical Chinese 猶豫 ('hesitation, indecision, delay' — traditionally explained via two cautious animals, 猶 and 豫, or as an alliterative binome *juw-jo* for wavering); in Japanese extended to 'postponement, grace period, reprieve'.

history.meaning: postponement; grace period; extension of time; hesitation

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 猶予
Wiktionary — 猶予 (Japanese)

玄関.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 玄 ('deep, profound') and 関 ('gate, barrier'). Originally a Zen Buddhist term for the gateway to profound teachings and the formal entry hall of a temple, it generalized to the entranceway of Japanese homes and inns where shoes are removed.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 玄関 (Japanese)

現金.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 現 ('present, on the spot, actual') and 金 ('money, gold'), literally 'money right in front of you' as opposed to credit or ledger accounts.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 現金 (Japanese)

理想.etymology: Meiji-era philosophical Sino-Japanese coinage 理想 (risō), introduced by Nishi Amane to translate Western *ideal*, combining 理 ('reason, principle, idea') + 想 ('conception, thought').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 理想
Wiktionary — 理想 (Japanese)

理由.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 理由 (riyū), from Classical Chinese 理由 ('underlying principle and cause/origin'), combining 理 ('principle, logic') + 由 ('cause, whence something comes').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 理由
Wiktionary — 理由 (Japanese)

瓶.etymology: Read both as Sino-Japanese *bin* (from Middle Chinese 瓶 *beng*, 'jug, pitcher, vase, bottle') and native Japanese *kame* (inherited from Old Japanese *kame₂* 'wide-mouthed earthenware jar or crock').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 瓶
Wiktionary — 瓶 (Japanese)

甘い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *amasi* (甘し, 'sweet-tasting, delicious, mildly salted, indulgent'), attested in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki; cognate with うまし (旨し・美し, 'savory, delicious').

history.meaning: sweet; lightly salted; lenient/indulgent; naive/optimistic; loose

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 甘い
Wiktionary — 甘い (Japanese)

生き物.etymology: Native Japanese compound *ikimono* combining いき (生き, continuative stem of 生きる 'to live') + もの (物・者, 'being, thing, creature'), attested from classical times.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 生き物
Wiktionary — 生き物 (Japanese)

生地.etymology: Hybrid compound read *kiji* (written 生地 or 素地), combining native Japanese き (生, 'raw, unworked, natural state') + Sino-Japanese じ (地, 'ground, base material, texture, fabric').

history.meaning: unadorned base material; natural state; unpainted wood or cloth
cloth; fabric; unbaked dough/batter; natural complexion/character

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 生地
Wiktionary — 生地 (Japanese)

生演奏.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native prefix 生- (なま-, 'unprocessed, live, in person') with Sino-Japanese 演奏 (えんそう, 'musical performance').
生演奏.notes: Contrasts live acoustic music with recorded playback.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 生演奏 (Japanese)

用.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 用 (yō), from Middle Chinese 用 (*jowngH*, 'use, employment, function, task, business, errand, expense').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 用
Wiktionary — 用 (Japanese)

用意.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 用意 (yōi), from Classical Chinese 用意 ('applying one's mind, mental attention, forethought'), which developed in Japanese from 'careful attention, precaution' into 'making preparations, getting ready'.

history.meaning: direct one's mind or intention; take care

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 用意
Wiktionary — 用意 (Japanese)

由香.etymology: Japanese feminine given name (commonly read Yuka) composed of 由 ('reason, origin, freedom') + 香 ('fragrance, incense, sweet scent').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 香
Wiktionary — 由香 (Japanese)

申し訳.etymology: Polite compound noun 申し訳 (mōshiwake), combining もうし (申し, humble verb stem 'to say, state') + わけ (訳, 'reason, explanation'), literally 'stating an explanation or excuse', used chiefly in 申し訳ない / 申し訳ありません ('I have no excuse -> I am deeply sorry').

history.meaning: explanation offered to clear oneself; apology

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 申し訳
Wiktionary — 申し訳 (Japanese)

男.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *woto₂ko₁* (男, 'young man, vigorous man, male'), a compound of *woto₂* ('young, youthful', compare *wotome* 乙女 'maiden') + *ko₁* (子・彦, 'person, lad'); replaced simple *wo* (夫・男) as the general noun for 'man'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 男
Wiktionary — 男 (Japanese)

男性.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 男性 (dansei / nansei), combining 男 ('male, man') + 性 ('sex, gender, nature'), serving in modern Japanese as the standard polite/formal noun for 'man, male'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 男性
Wiktionary — 男性 (Japanese)

町.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mati* (町, 'dividing path between rice paddies, partitioned plot of land, ward of a capital city'), which in medieval and early modern times came to denote a market street, townquarter, or town.

history.meaning: measured section of land or palace/capital ward

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 町
Wiktionary — 町 (Japanese)

画面.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 画面 (gamen), from Chinese 畫面 ('painted surface of a picture'), combining 画 (畫, 'painting, picture, image') + 面 ('surface, face'); extended in the 20th century to cinema, television, computer, and smartphone screens.

history.stage: Late Imperial Chinese / Early Modern Japanese
history.meaning: surface of a painting; picture plane
screen (of a TV, monitor, or phone); picture plane; scene

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 画面
Wiktionary — 画面 (Japanese)

留める.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb (read とめる or とどめる, 'to stop, fasten, detain, keep in place'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *tomu* (and expanded *todomu*), the transitive counterpart of *tomaru* (止まる / 留まる 'to come to a stop, remain'). Orthographically written with 留 when emphasizing keeping in place, fastening, or fixing.

history.form: 留める (とめる / とどめる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 留める
Wiktionary — 留める (Japanese)

留め金.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('clasp, latch, catch, metal fastener'), formed from 留め (とめ, nominalized stem of 留める 'to fasten, hold in place') + 金 (かね → がね with rendaku, 'metal, metal fitting').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 留め金
Wiktionary — 留め金 (Japanese)

留守.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun borrowed from Middle Chinese 留守 (*ljuw-sjuwX*, 'remaining behind to guard the capital or residence while the lord is away'), from 留 ('remain, stay') + 守 ('guard, protect'). Attested since the Heian period for watching over a house during the master's absence, and later shifted in everyday usage to denote the absence itself ('being away from home').

history.meaning: stay behind to guard a post or palace
caretaker duty during the master's absence

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 留守
Wiktionary — 留守 (Japanese)

留守番電話.etymology: Modern Sino-Japanese compound noun ('answering machine, voicemail'), combining 留守番 (るすばん 'house-sitting, minding the house while someone is out', from 留守 'absence' + 番 'watch, duty') + 電話 (でんわ 'telephone').

history.form: 留守番電話 (るすばんでんわ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 留守番電話
Wiktionary — 留守番電話 (Japanese)

番.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and counter borrowed from Middle Chinese 番 (*phjwon*, 'turn, rotation, watch duty, time'). Used in Japanese since the Heian period for a scheduled turn on guard or service duty, a position in sequence ('number'), or a match/round.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 番
Wiktionary — 番 (Japanese)

番号.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('assigned number, serial number, numeral designation'), formed from 番 (ばん 'sequential turn, order') + 号 (ごう 'designation, mark, number').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 番号
Wiktionary — 番号 (Japanese)

番地.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese administrative compound ('house number, lot number, street address number'), coined from 番 (ばん 'sequence number') + 地 (ち 'land, plot, lot') when numbered land-parcel addressing was instituted in the early Meiji period.

history.meaning: numbered land lot; street address number

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 番地
Wiktionary — 番地 (Japanese)

痛い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('painful, sore, aching'), continuing Old Japanese *itasi* (stem *ita-*), attested in the Man'yōshū; closely related to the intensive root *ita* / *ito* ('exceedingly, sorely, intensely').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 痛い
Wiktionary — 痛い (Japanese)

白い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('white, fair, blank'), continuing Old Japanese *sirosi* (stem *siro-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū for bright, clear white; cognate with 著し (*ichijirushi* 'conspicuous, clear') and 知る (*shiru* 'to perceive, know').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 白い
Wiktionary — 白い (Japanese)

白紙.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 白 ('white, unmarked') and 紙 ('paper'), denoting an unwritten sheet of paper and figuratively a clean slate.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 白紙 (Japanese)

白黒.etymology: Native Japanese dvandva (coordinative) compound noun ('black and white, monochrome; right and wrong, guilt and innocence'), formed from 白 (しろ 'white') + 黒 (くろ 'black').

history.meaning: white and black; monochrome; right and wrong

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 白黒
Wiktionary — 白黒 (Japanese)

百円.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-classifier compound ('one hundred yen'), formed from 百 (ひゃく 'one hundred', Middle Chinese *pæk*) + 円 (えん 'yen; round coin', adopted in 1871 as Japan's modern decimal currency unit).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 百
Wiktionary — 百円 (Japanese)

百回.etymology: Sino-Japanese numeral-counter compound ('one hundred times'), formed from 百 (ひゃく → ひゃっ with consonant assimilation before *k-*, 'one hundred') + 回 (かい 'time, turn, occurrence').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 回
Wiktionary — 百回 (Japanese)

的.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read まと, 'target, mark, bullseye'), continuing Old Japanese *mato*, attested in the Nihon Shoki and Wamyō Ruijūshō; traditionally analyzed as *ma-* (bound form of 目 'eye' or 間 'space') + *to* (処 'place, spot'), i.e. the spot aimed at with the eyes, written logographically with kanji 的 ('target, white mark').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 的
Wiktionary — 的 (Japanese)

皆さん.etymology: Polite plural pronoun and form of address ('everyone, all of you'), formed from native Japanese 皆 (みな 'all, everyone', Old Japanese *mina*) + polite honorific suffix -さん (reduced from 様 *-sama*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 皆さん
Wiktionary — 皆さん (Japanese)

皮.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('skin, hide, pelt, bark, peel, rind'), continuing Old Japanese *kapa*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū for the outer covering of bodies, trees, and fruits (orthographically distinguished from 革 'tanned leather' in modern usage, though sharing the same etymon).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 皮
Wiktionary — 皮 (Japanese)

監督.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('supervision, direction; director, manager, coach'), from Classical Chinese 監督 (attested in the Book of Later Han), composed of 監 (かん 'oversee, inspect from above') + 督 (とく 'supervise, command'). Adopted in modern Japanese for administrative supervisors, film directors, and team coaches.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 監督
Wiktionary — 監督 (Japanese)

目.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('eye; sight; mesh, grain; experience; ordinal suffix'), continuing Old Japanese *me₂* (alternating with bound prefix *ma-* in compounds like まぶた 'eyelid'), from Proto-Japonic *\*mai* ('eye').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 目
Wiktionary — 目 (Japanese)

目覚まし.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('alarm clock; waking up; eye-opener'), nominalized from the連用形 of 目覚ます (*mezamasu* 'to wake up, open one's eyes from sleep', from 目 'eye' + 覚ます 'to awaken'); in modern everyday use, frequently elliptical for 目覚まし時計 ('alarm clock').

history.meaning: waking from sleep; something striking that opens the eyes

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 目覚まし
Wiktionary — 目覚まし (Japanese)

直す.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to fix, repair, correct, restore, cure, alter'), continuing Old Japanese *naposu*, the transitive counterpart of *naporu* (直る 'to be restored, get better'), built on the root *napo-* ('straight, right, normal', seen in classical adjective 直し *naposi*).

history.meaning: make straight; restore to normal; correct

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 直す
Wiktionary — 直す (Japanese)

直せる.etymology: Potential verb ('to be able to fix, can repair, can correct'), formed as the regular *e*-grade potential derivative (*naos-e-ru*) of the consonant-stem (godan) transitive verb 直す (*naosu* 'to fix, repair, correct').

history.meaning: can fix; be able to repair or correct

morphemes.meaning: potential stem of 直す (fix, repair)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 直す
Wiktionary — 直せる (Japanese)

直る.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to be fixed, be repaired, be corrected, return to normal'), continuing Old Japanese *naporu*, derived from the root *napo-* ('straight, upright, normal', as in classical adjective 直し *naposi*).

history.meaning: be fixed; be repaired; be corrected

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 直る
Wiktionary — 直る (Japanese)

直接.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adverbial ('direct, immediate, firsthand'), formed from 直 (ちょく 'straight, unmediated, direct') + 接 (せつ 'touch, connect, come into contact'). Standardized in the Meiji period to render Western concepts of 'direct' (in contrast to 間接 'indirect').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 直接
Wiktionary — 直接 (Japanese)

相手.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('partner, companion, other party, opponent'), attested from the Heian period onward, formed from 相 (あい, from 合う 'to meet, face each other, match') + 手 (て 'hand; person filling a role or performing an action').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 相手
Wiktionary — 相手 (Japanese)

相棒.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('partner, buddy, sidekick, colleague'), originating in Edo-period palanquin-bearer (*kago*) jargon for the fellow bearer who shared the same carrying pole: formed from native 相 (あい 'mutual, fellow') + Sino-Japanese 棒 (ぼう 'carrying pole, staff'). Later generalized to any close partner or collaborator.

history.meaning: fellow bearer sharing a palanquin carrying pole

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 相棒

相談.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('consultation, discussion, talking things over'), formed from 相 (そう 'mutually, together') + 談 (だん 'talk, converse, discuss'). Attested in Japanese from the Muromachi period onward.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 相談
Wiktionary — 相談 (Japanese)

眉.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('eyebrow'), continuing Old Japanese *mayu*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; generally analyzed as containing the bound eye root *ma-* (目 'eye').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 眉

看板.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 看 ('look at, watch') and 板 ('wooden board'), originally a painted wooden shop board hung outside to catch passers-by's eyes.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 看板 (Japanese)

真っ白.etymology: Emphatic native Japanese adjectival noun ('pure white, snow-white, completely blank'), formed from intensive prefix 真- (ま- 'true, pure, complete', with expressive consonant gemination まっ-) + 白 (しろ 'white').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真っ白
Wiktionary — 真っ白 (Japanese)

真っ直ぐ.etymology: Emphatic native Japanese adjectival noun and adverb ('straight, direct, upright, honest'), formed from intensive prefix 真- (ま- with expressive gemination まっ-) + 直ぐ (すぐ 'straight, direct, upright', stem of classical adjective 直ぐし).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真っ直ぐ
Wiktionary — 真っ直ぐ (Japanese)

真ん中.etymology: Emphatic native Japanese compound noun ('exact center, dead center, right in the middle'), formed from intensive prefix 真- (ま- 'true, exact', with nasal insertion まん- before *n-*) + 中 (なか 'inside, middle, center').

history.form: まなか → まんなか (真ん中)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真ん中

真夜中.etymology: Native Japanese prefix 真- (ま-, 'true, exact, dead centre') + 夜中 (よなか, 'middle of the night': 夜 よ + 中 なか).

sources.title: Wiktionary — 真夜中 (Japanese)

真鍮.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 真 ('true, pure') and 鍮 ('brass, copper-zinc alloy'), attested from the Muromachi and Edo periods for golden-yellow brass hardware.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 真鍮 (Japanese)

真鍮バルブ.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and Western loanword compound ('brass valve'), combining 真鍮 (しんちゅう 'brass', borrowed from early modern Chinese 真鍮 for copper-zinc alloy) + バルブ (borrowed from English *valve*).

history.form: 真鍮バルブ (しんちゅうバルブ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真鍮
Wiktionary — 真鍮 (Japanese)

真鍮プレート.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and Western loanword compound ('brass plate, brass plaque'), combining 真鍮 (しんちゅう 'brass') + プレート (borrowed from English *plate*).

history.form: 真鍮プレート (しんちゅうプレート)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真鍮
Wiktionary — 真鍮 (Japanese)

真鍮ランプ.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and Western loanword compound ('brass lamp'), combining 真鍮 (しんちゅう 'brass') + ランプ (borrowed from Dutch *lamp* / English *lamp*).

history.form: 真鍮ランプ (しんちゅうランプ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 真鍮
Wiktionary — 真鍮 (Japanese)

眠る.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to sleep, fall asleep'), continuing Old Japanese *neburu* > Middle Japanese *nemuru*, derived from the sleep root *ne-* (seen in 寝 *ne* / 寝る *neru* 'to sleep, lie down') + verbal derivative element *-buru* / *-muru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 眠る

history.meaning: can sleep; be able to fall asleep

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 眠る

眺め.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('view, prospect, scenery, gazing'), nominalized from the連用形 of 眺める (*nagameru*, Old Japanese *nagamu* 'to gaze fixedly into the distance while lost in thought, look out over', related to 長し *nagasi* 'long' + 目 *me* 'eye' / 見 *mi* 'look').

history.meaning: pensive gazing into the distance; long rain

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 眺め

眼鏡.etymology: Jukujikun spelling pairing 眼 ('eye') + 鏡 ('mirror, lens') with native reading めがね (from 目 'eye' + 金 'metal frame').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 眼鏡 (Japanese)

着く.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to arrive, reach, touch, take a seat'), continuing Old Japanese *tuku* (four-grade *tuk-* 'to come into contact with, attach, reach a point'). Written with 着 for arriving at a destination or sitting down at a place (etymologically identical to 付く).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 着く
Wiktionary — 着く (Japanese)

着る.etymology: Native Japanese transitive upper monograde (kami-ichidan) verb ('to wear, put on [clothing on the upper or whole body]'), continuing Old Japanese *kiru* (stem *ki₁-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*ki-ru*.

history.meaning: put on; wear on the body

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 着る
Wiktionary — 着る (Japanese)

着地.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun and suru-verb ('landing, touching down on the ground'), formed from 着 (ちゃく 'arrive, reach, touch') + 地 (ち 'ground, earth').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 着地
Wiktionary — 着地 (Japanese)

着替える.etymology: Native Japanese compound verb ('to change clothes'), formed from the連用形 *ki* of 着る ('to wear, put on clothes') + 替える (かえる → がえる with rendaku, 'to exchange, replace, switch').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 着替える
Wiktionary — 着替える (Japanese)

矢印.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('arrow symbol, directional arrow mark'), formed from 矢 (や 'arrow', Old Japanese *ya*) + 印 (しるし → じるし with rendaku, 'mark, sign, emblem'). history.meaning: identifying mark on an arrow shaft

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 矢印

知らせ.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('notice, notification, news, report, omen'), nominalized from the連用形 of 知らせる (*shiraseru* 'to let know, inform, notify', causative of 知る *shiru* 'to know').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 知らせ
Wiktionary — 知らせ (Japanese)

知る.etymology: Native Japanese consonant-stem (godan) verb ('to know, come to know, learn, be aware of'), continuing Old Japanese *siru* (attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū with the dual senses 'to discern, know' and 'to rule, govern'); cognate with 白し (*sirosi* 'bright, clear') and 著し (*ichijirushi* 'conspicuous, manifest').

history.meaning: know; find out; become acquainted with

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 知る

短い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('short, brief'), continuing Old Japanese *mizikasi* (stem *mizika-*), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 短い
Wiktionary — 短い (Japanese)

石.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('stone, rock, pebble'), continuing Old Japanese *isi* (alongside variant *iso* 'rock, rocky shore'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*isi*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 石
Wiktionary — 石 (Japanese)

石壁.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 石 (いし, 'stone') and 壁 (かべ, 'wall').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 石壁 (Japanese)

石段.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('stone steps, stone stairway'), combining native 石 (いし 'stone') + Sino-Japanese 段 (だん 'step, stair, tier').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 石段
Wiktionary — 石段 (Japanese)

石畳.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('stone paving, cobblestone pavement, flagstone walk'), formed from 石 (いし 'stone') + 畳 (たたみ → だたみ with rendaku, nominalized from 畳む 'to fold, layer, lay flat side by side').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 石畳
Wiktionary — 石畳 (Japanese)

石鹸.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('soap'), read せっけん from the on'yomi of 石 ('stone, solid cake') + 鹸 ('alkali, lye, soda'). While soap introduced by the Portuguese in the 16th century was originally called シャボン (from Portuguese *sabão*), the Chinese-derived character compound 石鹸 read *sekken* became the standard term from the Meiji period onward.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 石鹸
Wiktionary — 石鹸 (Japanese)

石鹸水.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('soapy water, soapsuds'), formed from 石鹸 (せっけん 'soap') + 水 (すい 'water, liquid').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 石鹸水
Wiktionary — 石鹸水 (Japanese)

砂糖.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('sugar'), borrowed in the Muromachi period from Chinese 砂糖 / 沙糖 (Middle Chinese *sra-thang*, literally 'sand-like granular sugar'), composed of 砂 ('sand, grit') + 糖 ('sugar, sweet malt').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 砂糖

history.meaning: be torn; be broken; be defeated
tear; rip; be broken; be defeated

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 破れる

確か.etymology: Native Japanese adjectival noun and adverb ('certain, sure, reliable, accurate; if I remember rightly'), continuing Old and Heian Japanese *tasika* ('firm, secure, trustworthy, definite'), built on the root *tasi-* ('thorough, full, reliable') + adjectival suffix *-ka*.

history.meaning: certain; sure; reliable; if I recall

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 確か
Wiktionary — 確か (Japanese)

確かめる.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to ascertain, confirm, verify, make sure'), continuing classical lower bigrade *tasikamu* (確かむ), derived from the adjectival stem 確か (*tashika* 'certain, sure') + verbalizing suffix *-mu* > *-meru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 確かめる

確認.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('confirmation, verification, affirmation'), formed from 確 (かく 'firm, certain, definite') + 認 (にん 'recognize, acknowledge, verify').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 確認

磨く.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to polish, burnish, scrub, brush [teeth], cultivate [a skill]'), continuing Old Japanese *migaku*, attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 磨く
Wiktionary — 磨く (Japanese)

祈る.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to pray, invoke, wish earnestly'), continuing Old Japanese *inoru*, attested in the Man'yōshū; traditionally analyzed as sacred/ritual prefix *i-* (斎 'consecrated, taboo', as in 忌む *imu*) + 宣る (*noru* 'to proclaim or recite solemn ritual words').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 祈る

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 祖母
Wiktionary — 祖母 (Japanese)

祖父.etymology: Sino-Japanese kinship noun ('grandfather'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 祖父 (Middle Chinese *tsuX-bjuX*), composed of 祖 (そ 'ancestor, grandparent') + 父 (ふ 'father').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 祖父
Wiktionary — 祖父 (Japanese)

私.etymology: First-person pronoun ('I, me'), reduced in Early Modern Japanese from わたくし (私, originally a noun meaning 'private, personal, non-official matter' as opposed to 公 *ōyake* 'public, imperial court'). history.meaning: private affair; personal interest (vs. 公 public)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 私

私たち.etymology: First-person plural pronoun ('we, us'), formed from 私 (わたし 'I, me') + pluralizing personal suffix -たち (Old Japanese *-tati*, originally an honorific collective marker for deities and nobles).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 私たち
Wiktionary — 私たち (Japanese)

秋.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('autumn, fall'), continuing Old Japanese *aki₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; traditionally linked either to 飽き (*aki* 'fullness, abundance of ripened grain harvest') or 明き / 赤 (*aki* / *aka* 'clear, bright sky or crimson foliage').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 秋
Wiktionary — 秋 (Japanese)

秘密.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adjectival noun ('secret, secrecy, mystery'), borrowed from Chinese 秘密 (prominent in Buddhist scriptures translating Sanskrit *guhya* 'hidden, esoteric'), composed of 秘 (ひ 'conceal, keep secret') + 密 (みつ 'dense, covert, confidential').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 秘密
Wiktionary — 秘密 (Japanese)

移動.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 移動 (いどう), combining 移 ('shift, transfer') and 動 ('move').
