sources.title: Wiktionary — 移動 (Japanese)

稲妻.etymology: Poetic native compound 稲妻 (いなずま), combining 稲 (いな-, bound form of いね 'rice plant') and 妻 (つま, 'spouse, partner', voiced to -ずま by rendaku).
稲妻.notes: Coined in ancient Japan because late-summer lightning storms coincided with the ripening of rice ears, inspiring the belief that lightning wedded and fertilized the rice crop.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 稲妻 (Japanese)

穏やか.etymology: Native Japanese adjectival noun ('calm, gentle, peaceful, quiet, moderate'), attested from the Heian period as *odayaka* (alongside *odahi* 'tranquil'), formed from the root *oda-* ('calm, settled') + descriptive suffix *-yaka*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 穏やか

空.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read そら, 'sky, heavens, air; weather; from memory'), continuing Old Japanese *sora*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*sora* ('sky, open space above'). sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 空

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 空く
Wiktionary — 空く (Japanese)

空っぽ.etymology: Colloquial native Japanese noun and adjectival noun ('completely empty, hollow'), formed in Early Modern Japanese from 空 (から 'empty, hollow, shell') + emphatic colloquial suffix -っぽ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 空っぽ
Wiktionary — 空っぽ (Japanese)

空気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('air, atmosphere; mood of a situation'), formed from 空 (くう 'sky, open space, void') + 気 (き 'breath, vapor, gas, vital energy'). Standardized in late Edo Dutch studies (Rangaku) to translate Dutch *lucht* ('air, atmosphere').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 空気
Wiktionary — 空気 (Japanese)

空間.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('space, room, expanse'), formed from 空 (くう 'empty, open, void') + 間 (かん 'interval, space between'). Used in classical Chinese for an open gap and standardized in Meiji philosophy and physics to translate English *space* and German *Raum*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 空間
Wiktionary — 空間 (Japanese)

窓.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('window'), continuing Old Japanese *mado*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Wamyō Ruijūshō; a compound of 間 (*ma* 'space, interval') or 目 (*ma-* 'eye, opening') + 戸 (*to* → *do* with rendaku, 'door, shutter, opening').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 窓
Wiktionary — 窓 (Japanese)

窓ガラス.etymology: Hybrid native Japanese and Western loanword compound ('windowpane, window glass'), combining native 窓 (まど 'window') + ガラス ('glass', borrowed in the Edo period from Dutch *glas*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 窓ガラス
Wiktionary — 窓ガラス (Japanese)

窓際.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('by the window, windowside, edge of a window'), formed from 窓 (まど 'window') + 際 (きわ → ぎわ with rendaku, 'edge, brink, side').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 窓際
Wiktionary — 窓際 (Japanese)

立つ.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to stand, rise, be erected, depart'), continuing Old Japanese *tatu* (four-grade *tat-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, paired with transitive *tatu* (lower bigrade > 立てる *tateru*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 立つ
Wiktionary — 立つ (Japanese)

立てかける.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to lean [something] against, prop up against'), formed from 立て (stem of 立てる 'to stand up, set upright') + かける (掛ける 'to hang, rest, or suspend against another surface').

history.form: 立てかける (たてかける)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 立て掛ける
Wiktionary — 立てかける (Japanese)

端.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read はし, は, or はた, 'edge, end, tip, border, margin'), continuing Old Japanese *pasi* ('extremity, tip, edge') and *pata* ('edge, rim, side').

history.form: 端 (はし / は / はた)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 端
Wiktionary — 端 (Japanese)

端っこ.etymology: Colloquial native Japanese noun ('very edge, tip, corner, far end'), formed from 端 (はし 'edge, end, tip') + familiar/diminutive nominal suffix -っこ.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 端っこ
Wiktionary — 端っこ (Japanese)

競争.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese compound noun and suru-verb ('competition, contest, rivalry'), coined by Fukuzawa Yukichi in the 1860s to translate English *competition* by combining 競 (きょう 'vie, race, compete') + 争 (そう 'contend, strive').

history.meaning: competition (coined by Fukuzawa Yukichi for English competition)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 競争
Wiktionary — 競争 (Japanese)

笑う.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to laugh, smile'), continuing Old Japanese *warapu*, attested in the Man'yōshū; built on the root *wara-* ('split open, burst open', shared with 割る *waru* 'to split'), originally describing the mouth or face opening wide in laughter.

history.meaning: laugh aloud; open the mouth in laughter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 笑う
Wiktionary — 笑う (Japanese)

笑顔.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('smiling face, smile'), formed from the stem *e-* of classical 笑む (*emu*, Old Japanese *wemu* 'to smile, bloom') + 顔 (かお → がお with rendaku, 'face, countenance').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 笑顔
Wiktionary — 笑顔 (Japanese)

笠.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('conical woven hat of bamboo or sedge; lamp shade; mushroom cap'), continuing Old Japanese *kasa*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū (etymologically identical to 傘 'umbrella, parasol', both denoting an overhead protective cover against rain or sun).

history.meaning: conical sedge/bamboo hat; lamp shade; cap

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 笠
Wiktionary — 笠 (Japanese)

第十四条.etymology: Sino-Japanese legal and statutory compound ('Article 14'), formed from ordinal prefix 第- (だい-) + 十四 (じゅうよん / じゅうし 'fourteen') + 条 (じょう 'article, clause, provision in a law or contract').

history.form: 第十四条 (だいじゅうよんじょう)
history.meaning: Article 14 (of a law, regulation, or contract)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 条
Wiktionary — 条 (Japanese)

箱.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('box, case, chest, container'), continuing Old Japanese *pako₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 箱
Wiktionary — 箱 (Japanese)

築八十年.etymology: Sino-Japanese architectural and real-estate compound ('built eighty years ago, eighty years old [of a building]'), formed from 築 (ちく 'construction, years elapsed since construction') + 八十年 (はちじゅうねん 'eighty years').

history.form: 築八十年 (ちくはちじゅうねん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 築
Wiktionary — 築 (Japanese)

簡単.etymology: Sino-Japanese adjectival noun ('simple, easy, brief, uncomplicated'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 簡単 (attested in the Zuo Zhuan and Book of Han), composed of 簡 (かん 'bamboo slip; concise, abridged, simple') + 単 (たん 'single, uncompounded, simple').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 簡単
Wiktionary — 簡単 (Japanese)

粉砂糖.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('powdered sugar, confectioners' sugar, icing sugar'), combining native 粉 (こな 'powder, flour') + Sino-Japanese 砂糖 (さとう → ざとう with rendaku, 'sugar').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 粉砂糖
Wiktionary — 粉砂糖 (Japanese)

約束.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('promise, appointment, agreement, stipulation'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 約束 ('bind together, restrain, stipulate'), composed of 約 (やく 'bind, tie, covenant') + 束 (そく 'tie in a bundle, restrain').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 約束
Wiktionary — 約束 (Japanese)

紅茶.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 紅 ('crimson, deep red') and 茶 ('tea'), named after the coppery-red color of oxidized black tea liquor (just as Chinese hóngchá literally means 'red tea').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 紅茶 (Japanese)

紙.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('paper'), continuing Old Japanese *kami₂*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Nihon Shoki.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 紙
Wiktionary — 紙 (Japanese)

紙やすり.etymology: Native compound of 紙 (かみ, 'paper') and やすり (鑢, 'metal file or rasp').
紙やすり.notes: Literally a 'paper file'—heavy paper coated with abrasive grit for smoothing wood before painting.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 紙やすり (Japanese)

素敵.etymology: Adjectival noun ('lovely, wonderful, great, nice'), arising in late Edo colloquial speech as すてき (written ateji as 素敵 or 素適); commonly explained either as intensive prefix 素- (す-) + 出来 (でき 'fine workmanship/result') or 敵 (てき 'matchless'), or as a phonological blend related to 素晴らしい. Originally meant 'extreme, tremendous' before narrowing to 'wonderful, charming'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 素敵
Wiktionary — 素敵 (Japanese)

素晴らしい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('wonderful, splendid, magnificent, superb'), attested from the Edo period as *subarasii*, formed by adding the intensive prefix 素- (*su-* 'pure, utter, sheer') to an older adjective *barasii* / *harasii* (originally 'extreme, tremendous', shifting in Modern Japanese to positive admiration).

history.form: すばらしい (素晴らしい)
素晴らしい (すばらしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 素晴らしい
Wiktionary — 素晴らしい (Japanese)

素直.etymology: Native Japanese adjectival noun ('honest, frank, gentle, obedient, straightforward'), formed in Late Middle / Early Modern Japanese from prefix 素- (す- 'plain, unadorned, natural') + 直 (なお 'straight, upright, unwarped', from Old Japanese *napo*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 素直
Wiktionary — 素直 (Japanese)

細い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('thin, slender, narrow, fine'), continuing Old Japanese *pososi* (stem *poso-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 細い
Wiktionary — 細い (Japanese)

細かい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('small, fine, minute, detailed'), formed in Early Modern Japanese by adding the adjectival inflection -い to the classical adjectival noun 細か (*komaka* 'fine-grained, small, detailed', attested from the Heian period, built on root *koma-* 'small, fine' + suffix *-ka*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 細かい
Wiktionary — 細かい (Japanese)

細める.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to narrow [one's eyes], make thinner, reduce'), continuing classical lower bigrade *posomu* (細む), derived from the adjective stem 細- (*hoso-* 'thin, narrow') + transitive verbalizing suffix *-mu* > *-meru*.

history.meaning: narrow (one's eyes); make thinner; turn down

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 細める
Wiktionary — 細める (Japanese)

紳士.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('gentleman'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 紳士 ('girdled officials and scholars of high standing', from 紳 'ceremonial sash worn by officials' + 士 'scholar, gentleman') and standardized in the Meiji period to translate English *gentleman*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 紳士
Wiktionary — 紳士 (Japanese)

紳士靴.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and native Japanese compound noun ('men's shoes, gentleman's dress shoes'), combining Sino-Japanese 紳士 (しんし 'gentleman, men's') + native 靴 (くつ → ぐつ with rendaku, 'shoes').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 紳士
Wiktionary — 紳士 (Japanese)

紺色.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and native Japanese compound noun ('navy blue, dark indigo blue'), combining Sino-Japanese 紺 (こん 'deep dark blue tinged with violet-red', Middle Chinese 紺 *khamH*) + native 色 (いろ 'color').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 紺色
Wiktionary — 紺色 (Japanese)

終わり.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('end, conclusion, close, termination'), nominalized from the連用形 of 終わる (*owaru*, Old Japanese *woparu* 'to come to an end, finish').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 終わり
Wiktionary — 終わり (Japanese)

終わる.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to end, finish, come to a close'), continuing Old Japanese *woparu*, the intransitive counterpart of lower bigrade *wopu* (終ふ > 終える *oeru* 'to bring to an end, complete').

history.meaning: come to an end; be completed

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 終わる
Wiktionary — 終わる (Japanese)

経る.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to pass through, elapse, experience, undergo'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *pu* (経, stem *pe₂-* 'to pass through time or places; to run warp threads on a loom').

history.meaning: pass through time or space; string warp threads

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 経る
Wiktionary — 経る (Japanese)

絵.etymology: Early Sino-Japanese borrowing from Middle Chinese 絵 / 繪 (*hwojH* > Old/Heian Japanese *we* > modern *e*, originally 'multicolored embroidery or painting'), fully naturalized in Japanese for any picture, drawing, painting, or illustration.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 絵
Wiktionary — 絵 (Japanese)

絵葉書.etymology: Compound noun ('picture postcard'), formed in the Meiji period from 絵 (え 'picture, illustration') + 葉書 (はがき 'postcard', from native 葉 'leaf, slip' + 書き 'writing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 絵葉書
Wiktionary — 絵葉書 (Japanese)

絶対.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun, adjectival noun, and adverb ('absolute, unconditional; absolutely, without fail'), originating in Buddhist Chinese 絶対 ('severing all opposition or comparison; beyond relativity', from 絶 'cut off, sever' + 対 'pair, opposite, comparison') and adopted in Meiji philosophy to translate Western *absolute* (contrasted with 相対 'relative').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 絶対
Wiktionary — 絶対 (Japanese)

継ぎ目.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('seam, joint, splice, juncture'), formed from 継ぎ (つぎ, nominalized stem of 継ぐ 'to join, patch, splice together') + 目 (め 'point, line, or crease where things meet').

history.meaning: seam; joint; juncture where two pieces meet

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 継ぎ目
Wiktionary — 継ぎ目 (Japanese)

続ける.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to continue, keep up, carry on, place in succession'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *tuduku* (続くる), the transitive counterpart of four-grade intransitive 続く (*tsuzuku* 'to continue, follow in a row').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 続ける
Wiktionary — 続ける (Japanese)

網.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('net, netting, mesh, web'), continuing Old Japanese *ami₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; closely related to the verb 編む (*amu* 'to plait, braid, knit, weave a net').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 網
Wiktionary — 網 (Japanese)

緊張.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('tension, strain, nervousness, tautness'), formed from 緊 (きん 'bind tightly, taut, pressing') + 張 (ちょう 'stretch, draw a bowstring taut').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 緊張
Wiktionary — 緊張 (Japanese)

緊急.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adjectival noun ('urgent, pressing, emergency'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 緊急 (attested in the History of the Southern Dynasties), composed of 緊 (きん 'tight, pressing, taut') + 急 (きゅう 'urgent, sudden, rapid').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 緊急
Wiktionary — 緊急 (Japanese)

緑.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('green, greenery, verdure'), continuing Old Japanese *midori*, attested in the Man'yōshū; originally denoting fresh, supple new shoots and buds sprouting in spring (cognate with 瑞 *mizu* 'fresh, moist, youthful'), and shifting in the Heian period to name the color green.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 緑
Wiktionary — 緑 (Japanese)

緑色.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('green color, green'), formed from 緑 (みどり 'green, fresh verdure') + 色 (いろ 'color').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 緑色
Wiktionary — 緑色 (Japanese)

締める.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to tie, fasten, tighten, constrict, shut, sum up'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *simu* (締む), the transitive counterpart of 締まる (*shimaru* 'to tighten, become taut or fastened').

history.meaning: tie; tighten; fasten; buckle; total up

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 締める
Wiktionary — 締める (Japanese)

締め出す.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to lock out, shut out, exclude'), formed from 締め (しめ, stem of 締める / 閉める 'to shut, lock, fasten') + 出す (だす 'to put out, drive out').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 締め出す
Wiktionary — 締め出す (Japanese)

緩む.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to loosen, slacken, come untied, relax, abate'), continuing Heian Japanese *yurumu*, derived from the root *yuru-* ('loose, slack, gentle', seen in 緩い *yurui*) + intransitive verbal suffix *-mu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 緩む
Wiktionary — 緩む (Japanese)

練習.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('practice, training, drill, exercise'), formed from 練 (れん 'refine silk by boiling; polish, train, drill') + 習 (しゅう 'flap wings repeatedly; practice, learn by repetition').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 練習
Wiktionary — 練習 (Japanese)

縁石.etymology: Compound noun ('curbstone, edging stone, border stone'), read either Sino-Japanese えんせき or native へりいし, composed of 縁 ('edge, rim, border') + 石 ('stone').

history.form: 縁石 (えんせき / へりいし)
history.meaning: border stone; curbstone along a road or walkway

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 縁石
Wiktionary — 縁石 (Japanese)

織物.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('woven fabric, textile, cloth'), attested since the Heian period, formed from 織り (おり, nominalized stem of 織る *oru* 'to weave', Old Japanese *woru*) + 物 (もの 'thing, article, goods').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 織物
Wiktionary — 織物 (Japanese)

繰り返す.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to repeat, do over again, reiterate'), formed from 繰り (くり, stem of 繰る *kuru* 'to reel in, draw a thread or cord hand over hand') + 返す (かえす 'to turn back, return, do over').

history.meaning: reel a cord back and forth; repeat over and over

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 繰り返す
Wiktionary — 繰り返す (Japanese)

缶.etymology: Early modern loanword (read かん, 'can, tin'), borrowed in the late Edo / early Meiji period from Dutch *kan* ('jug, pot, tin canister'; cf. English *can*) and written with the kanji 缶 (originally an ancient Chinese earthenware jar, Sino-Japanese *fu*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 缶
Wiktionary — 缶 (Japanese)

罠.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('trap, snare, pitfall'), continuing Old Japanese *wana*, attested in the Man'yōshū for a looped cord or noose set to catch game or birds; traditionally linked to 輪 (*wa* 'ring, loop') + 縄 (*nawa* 'rope, cord').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 罠
Wiktionary — 罠 (Japanese)

置く.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to put, place, set down, leave behind, establish'), continuing Old Japanese *oku* (four-grade *ok-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: set down; place; leave behind; settle (of dew/frost)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 置く
Wiktionary — 置く (Japanese)

署名.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('signature, signing one's name, autograph'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 署名, composed of 署 (しょ 'write down, inscribe officially') + 名 (めい 'name').

history.meaning: inscribe one's name on a document

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 署名
Wiktionary — 署名 (Japanese)

羊毛.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 羊毛 (ようもう), combining 羊 ('sheep') and 毛 ('hair, fleece, wool').
羊毛.notes: Dense compressed sheep's wool (羊毛フェルト) gives piano hammers their warm, rounded strike.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 羊毛 (Japanese)

美しい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('beautiful, lovely, fine'), continuing Old Japanese *utukusi*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, where it originally meant tender, doting affection felt toward a spouse, child, or small delicate creature ('dear, adorable, precious', cognate with 慈しむ *itsukushimu* 'to love tenderly'), before broadening from the Heian period onward to general aesthetic beauty.

history.form: うつくし (美し / 愛し)
history.meaning: dear; adorable; lovable (of family or small things)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 美しい
Wiktionary — 美しい (Japanese)

美央.etymology: Japanese female given name (read みお), formed from 美 (み 'beauty, beautiful', from the native stem seen in 美しい / 御) + 央 (お 'center, heart, middle').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 美
Wiktionary — 美 (Japanese)

羽根板.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 羽根 (はね, 'feather, wing-like blade') and 板 (いた, 'wooden board').
羽根板.notes: Describes angled overlapping wooden slats on louvred shutters.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 羽根板 (Japanese)

老眼鏡.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 老眼鏡 (ろうがんきょう), joining 老眼 ('farsightedness of age') with 鏡 ('mirror, optical lens').
老眼鏡.notes: Shares 眼鏡 ('glasses, spectacles') with everyday めがね.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 老眼鏡 (Japanese)

耳.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('ear; hearing; selvedge or crust edge'), continuing Old Japanese *mimi₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*mimi* ('ear').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 耳
Wiktionary — 耳 (Japanese)

聞く.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to hear, listen to; ask, inquire; grant'), continuing Old Japanese *kiku* (four-grade *kik-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 聞く
Wiktionary — 聞く (Japanese)

聞こえる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to be heard, be audible, sound; be renowned'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *kikoyu* (聞こゆ), derived from the verb root *kik-* (聞く 'to hear') + archaic mediopassive/spontaneous suffix *-oyu* > *-oeru*.

history.meaning: be audible; sound; become known; say humbly

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 聞こえる
Wiktionary — 聞こえる (Japanese)

聴く.etymology: Orthographic specification of native Japanese *kiku* (Old Japanese *kiku* 'to hear, listen'), written with the kanji 聴 ('listen attentively, heed') when emphasizing active, deliberate, or appreciative listening (such as listening to music or a speech).

history.meaning: listen attentively (to music, radio, or a speaker)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 聞く
Wiktionary — 聴く (Japanese)

肩.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('shoulder'), continuing Old Japanese *kata*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*kata* ('shoulder').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 肩
Wiktionary — 肩 (Japanese)

育つ.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to grow up, be raised, be brought up'), attested from Late Old / Heian Japanese as *sodatu* (paired with transitive 育てる *sodateru*); traditionally connected with 巣立つ (*sudatsu* 'for young birds to fledge and leave the nest', from 巣 'nest' + 立つ 'stand/rise').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 育つ
Wiktionary — 育つ (Japanese)

育てる.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to raise, rear, bring up, nurture, cultivate'), continuing classical lower bigrade *sodatu* (育つ, stem *sodate-*), the transitive counterpart of four-grade intransitive 育つ (*sodatsu* 'to grow up').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 育てる
Wiktionary — 育てる (Japanese)

背.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('back, spine; stature, height; mountain ridge'), continuing Old Japanese *se* (alternating with bound form *so-* in compounds like *somuku* 'turn one's back'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: back of the body; rear; ridge

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 背
Wiktionary — 背 (Japanese)

胸.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('chest, breast, bosom; heart, mind, feelings'), continuing Old Japanese *mune* (alternating with bound form *muna-* in compounds like 胸元 *munamoto*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 胸
Wiktionary — 胸 (Japanese)

脚.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read あし, 'leg [of a person, animal, or piece of furniture]; gait'), continuing Old Japanese *asi* ('foot, leg, step'), written specifically with the kanji 脚 when distinguishing the lower limb or supporting leg from the foot proper (足).

history.meaning: leg (of a body, table, or chair)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 足
Wiktionary — 脚 (Japanese)

脚立.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 脚 ('leg, support') and 立 ('stand'), originally a standing wooden trestle or footstool and now the standard word for a folding A-frame stepladder.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 脚立 (Japanese)

脱がせる.etymology: Causative transitive verb ('to undress [someone], take off [someone's clothes], make/let someone take off'), formed from the *a*-stem of 脱ぐ (*nugu* 'to take off clothes, undress') + causative suffix *-seru*.

history.meaning: undress someone; make/let someone take off clothes

morphemes.meaning: irrealis stem of 脱ぐ (take off clothes)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 脱ぐ
Wiktionary — 脱ぐ (Japanese)

脱ぐ.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to take off [clothes, shoes, or headgear], undress, strip off'), continuing Old Japanese *nuku* / *nugu*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with 抜く (*nuku* 'to pull out, extract, slip out of').

history.meaning: strip off; slip out of garments or footwear

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 脱ぐ
Wiktionary — 脱ぐ (Japanese)

腕.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('arm; skill, ability, competence'), continuing Old Japanese *ude*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Nihon Shoki; traditionally analyzed as *u-te* ('upper part of the hand/arm', from *u-* 'upper' + 手 *te* 'hand/arm' with sequential voicing).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 腕
Wiktionary — 腕 (Japanese)

腕時計.etymology: Compound noun ('wristwatch'), formed from native 腕 (うで 'arm, wrist') + 時計 (とけい → どけい with rendaku, Sino-Japanese 'clock, watch').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 腕時計
Wiktionary — 腕時計 (Japanese)

腫れる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to swell, become inflamed, puff up'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *paru* (腫る, stem *pare-*), related to four-grade 張る (*haru* 'to stretch, swell, become taut').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 腫れる
Wiktionary — 腫れる (Japanese)

膝.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('knee, lap'), continuing Old Japanese *piza*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Wamyō Ruijūshō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 膝
Wiktionary — 膝 (Japanese)

膨らむ.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to swell, expand, bulge, puff out'), continuing Heian–Middle Japanese *fukuramu* (alongside lower bigrade *fukuru* > 膨れる *fukureru*), built on the root *fukura-* ('puffed, soft and rounded', related to 袋 *fukuro* 'bag') + verbal suffix *-mu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 膨らむ
Wiktionary — 膨らむ (Japanese)

臆病.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adjectival noun ('cowardice, timidity; cowardly, timid'), attested in Japanese from the Kamakura period (frequently written 憶病 in medieval texts), composed of 臆 (おく 'chest, timid heart, cower') + 病 (びょう 'illness, affliction, weakness').

history.form: おくびやう (臆病 / 憶病)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 臆病

history.meaning: be packed full; be blocked; reach the end

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 詰まる

話.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('talk, speech, story, conversation, account'), nominalized from the連用形 of 話す (*hanasu* 'to speak, tell, converse').

話す.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to speak, talk, tell, converse'), emerging in Late Middle Japanese as a semantic specialization of 放す / 離す (*hanasu* 'to release, let loose, set free', Old Japanese *panasu*), from the metaphor of 'releasing words or thoughts from the mind'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 話す
Wiktionary — 話す (Japanese)

詳しい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('detailed, thorough, well-informed, well-versed'), continuing Old Japanese *kupasi* (stem *kupa-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, where it originally meant 'delicately beautiful, finely crafted, exquisite' before shifting to 'minutely detailed, thoroughly knowledgeable'.

history.form: くはし (細し / 詳し / 麗し)

誇らしい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('proud, triumphant'), attested from the Heian period as *hokorasi*, derived from the verb 誇る (*hokoru* 'to boast, take pride in, flourish') + adjectival suffix *-rashi* / *-ashii*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 誇らしい

誤る.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to make a mistake, err, be misled'), continuing Old Japanese *ayamaru*, attested in the Nihon Shoki (etymologically the same verb as 謝る 'to apologize', which developed from 'admit one's error and beg pardon').

history.form: あやまる (誤る / 過る)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 誤る

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 説明

読みやすい.etymology: Native Japanese compound adjective ('easy to read, legible, readable'), formed from 読み (よみ, stem of 読む 'to read') + やすい (易い 'easy to do').

history.form: 読みやすい (よみやすい)

読む.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to read, recite, chant; count; predict'), continuing Old Japanese *yomu* (four-grade *yom-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, where its primary sense was 'to count aloud one by one, enumerate' and hence 'to pronounce written characters in sequence or chant a text'.

history.meaning: count aloud; enumerate; recite a text

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 読む
Wiktionary — 読む (Japanese)

読書.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('reading books'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 読書 (Middle Chinese *duwk-syo*), composed of 読 (どく 'read aloud, study') + 書 (しょ 'book, writing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 読書

history.form: 読書ランプ (どくしょランプ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 誰

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 誰か

誰も.etymology: Inclusive and negative-polarity personal pronoun ('everyone, anyone; [with negative] no one, nobody'), formed from interrogative pronoun 誰 (だれ 'who') + inclusive particle も ('also, even').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 誰も
Wiktionary — 誰も (Japanese)

調.etymology: As Sino-Japanese ちょう ('musical key, tonality, tune, tone, style'), borrowed from Middle Chinese 調 (*dew* / *dewH* 'harmonize, musical mode, melody'); as native しらべ ('melody, tune; investigation'), nominalized from 調べる (*shiraberu* 'to tune strings, examine').

history.meaning: harmonize; musical mode or key; melody
musical key; tone; style / melody; inquiry

調べる.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to examine, investigate, check, look up; tune or play a musical instrument'), continuing Heian lower bigrade *sirabu* (調ぶ, stem *sirabe-* 'to harmonize musical tones, match and verify'), related to 知る (*shiru* 'to know, discern').

history.meaning: tune and play an instrument; verify; investigate

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 調べる

sources.title: Wiktionary — 調律 (Japanese)

調査.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('investigation, survey, inquiry, inspection'), composed of 調 (ちょう 'examine, harmonize, check') + 査 (さ 'inspect, look into, verify').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 調査

調査員.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('investigator, inspector, surveyor, examiner'), formed from 調査 (ちょうさ 'investigation, survey') + suffix -員 (-いん 'member, staff, official').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 貸す

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 賢明

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 赤い

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 足りる

sources.title: Wiktionary — 足首 (Japanese)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 踊り場

踏み台.etymology: Hybrid compound of native 踏み (ふみ, masu-stem of 踏む 'to step on') and Sino-Japanese 台 (だい, 'platform, stand').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 踏み台 (Japanese)

車.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('wheel; cart, carriage, vehicle, car'), continuing Old Japanese *kuruma*, attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū; derived from the verb root *kuru* (繰る / 転る 'to turn round and round, revolve') + nominal suffix *-ma*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 車

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 車輪
Wiktionary — 車輪 (Japanese)

軽い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('light [in weight], not heavy; slight, minor, nimble'), continuing Old Japanese *karusi* (stem *karu-* / *karo-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 軽い

軽やか.etymology: Native Japanese adjectival noun ('light, nimble, buoyant, sprightly'), attested from the Heian period as *karoyaka*, formed from the older bound stem *karo-* of 軽い ('light') + descriptive suffix *-yaka*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 軽やか
Wiktionary — 軽やか (Japanese)

輪.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('ring, circle, hoop, wheel, loop'), continuing Old Japanese *wa*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Wamyō Ruijūshō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 輪
Wiktionary — 輪 (Japanese)

辺り.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('neighborhood, vicinity, surroundings, area around'), nominalized from the連用形 of 当たる (*ataru* 'to touch upon, face, correspond to a place', Old Japanese *ataru*).

welcome; greet; meet; reach (a season or milestone)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 迎える

近く.etymology: Native Japanese noun and adverb ('nearness, neighborhood, vicinity; nearly, shortly'), substantivized from the連用形 (adverbial form) *chikaku* of the adjective 近い (*chikai*, Old Japanese *tikasi* 'near, close').

近づける.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to bring close, allow near, let approach'), continuing classical lower bigrade *tikaduku* (近づく), the transitive counterpart of four-grade intransitive 近づく (*chikazuku* 'to approach, draw near', from 近い stem *chika-* + 付く / 着く *tsuku*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 近づける

近所.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('neighborhood, vicinity, neighbors'), formed from 近 (きん 'near, close') + 所 (じょ, go-on reading of 所 'place, locality').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 近所

返す.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to return, give back, put back; turn over'), continuing Old Japanese *kapesu*, the transitive counterpart of 返る / 帰る (*kaeru* < *kaperu* 'to turn back, return').

返金.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun and suru-verb ('refund, repayment, returning money'), formed from 返 (へん 'return, give back') + 金 (きん 'money, gold').

迷い込む.etymology: Native Japanese compound intransitive verb ('to stray into, wander into, lose one's way and enter'), formed from 迷い (まよい, stem of 迷う 'to lose one's way, wander') + 込む (こむ 'to go into, enter deeply').

追い返す.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to drive back, turn away, send packing, repulse'), formed from 追い (おい, stem of 追う 'to chase, drive away') + 返す (かえす 'to send back, turn back').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 退屈

送る.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to send, dispatch; see off, escort; spend [time]'), continuing Old Japanese *okuru*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.
