sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 送る
Wiktionary — 送る (Japanese)

逃げる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to flee, run away, escape'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *nigu* (逃ぐ, stem *nige₂-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, paired with transitive 逃がす (*nigasu*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 逃げる
Wiktionary — 逃げる (Japanese)

逃げ出す.etymology: Native Japanese compound intransitive verb ('to run away, bolt, break into flight, flee from a place'), formed from 逃げ (にげ, stem of 逃げる 'to flee, run away') + 出す (だす 'to go out, burst forth, begin suddenly').

history.meaning: flee out of a place; bolt; start running away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 逃げ出す
Wiktionary — 逃げ出す (Japanese)

途中.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('on the way, midway, en route, in the middle of'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 途中, composed of 途 (と 'road, way, route') + 中 (ちゅう 'middle, in the course of').

history.meaning: on the way; midway; in the middle of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 途中
Wiktionary — 途中 (Japanese)

通す.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to let pass, pass through, pierce, usher in, persist in'), continuing Old Japanese *toposu*, the transitive counterpart of 通る (*tōru* < *toporu* 'to pass through').

history.meaning: cause to pass through; pierce; continue to the end
let pass; pass through; show in; persist in

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 通す
Wiktionary — 通す (Japanese)

通り.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('street, avenue, road; passage, flow; manner, way'), nominalized from the連用形 of 通る (*tōru* < Old Japanese *toporu* 'to pass along, go through').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 通り
Wiktionary — 通り (Japanese)

通り過ぎる.etymology: Native Japanese compound verb ('to pass by, go past'), formed from 通り (とおり, stem of 通る 'to pass along') + 過ぎる (すぎる 'to pass beyond, exceed').

history.form: 通り過ぎる (とおりすぎる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 通り過ぎる
Wiktionary — 通り過ぎる (Japanese)

通る.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to pass by, go through, pass [an exam], be accepted'), continuing Old Japanese *toporu*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: pass all the way through; penetrate
pass by; go through; pass (a test); carry (of a voice)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 通る
Wiktionary — 通る (Japanese)

速い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('fast, quick, rapid, speedy'), continuing Old Japanese *payasi* (stem *paya-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū (sharing the same native etymon as 早い 'early', written specifically with 速 for speed of motion or action).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 速い
Wiktionary — 速い (Japanese)

連れる.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to take along, bring [a person or animal] with one, be accompanied by'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *turu* (連る, stem *ture-* 'to form a companion group, go together'), derived from the root 連 (*tsura* / *tsure* 'row, line, companion').

history.meaning: go in company; line up together; take along
take along; bring with one; accompany

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 連れる
Wiktionary — 連れる (Japanese)

連絡.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('contact, communication, connection, liaison'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 連絡 / 聯絡 ('join and bind together in a continuous network'), composed of 連 (れん 'link, join in a row') + 絡 (らく 'entwine, connect threads').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 連絡
Wiktionary — 連絡 (Japanese)

週.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and counter ('week'), adopted in the Meiji period from Chinese 週 / 周 (しゅう 'cycle, circuit, full turn') when the seven-day Western calendar week was officially introduced.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 週
Wiktionary — 週 (Japanese)

週末.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('weekend'), coined in Modern Japanese as a calque of English *weekend*, from 週 (しゅう 'week') + 末 (まつ 'end, close').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 週末
Wiktionary — 週末 (Japanese)

進歩.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('progress, advancement, improvement'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 進歩 ('step forward, advance one's pace', from 進 'advance, move forward' + 歩 'step, pace') and standardized in the Meiji period to translate English *progress*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 進歩
Wiktionary — 進歩 (Japanese)

遅い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('slow; late'), continuing Old Japanese *ososi* (stem *oso-*), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 遅い
Wiktionary — 遅い (Japanese)

遅刻.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suru-verb ('lateness, tardiness, arriving past the appointed time'), formed from 遅 (ち 'late, slow, delayed') + 刻 (こく 'appointed time, hour').

history.meaning: arriving past the appointed hour; tardiness

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 遅刻
Wiktionary — 遅刻 (Japanese)

運び.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('carrying, transport; pace, progress, stage of arrangements'), nominalized from the連用形 of 運ぶ (*hakobu* 'to carry, transport, move forward').

history.meaning: carrying; movement of steps; progress of an affair

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 運び
Wiktionary — 運び (Japanese)

運ぶ.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to carry, transport, bear; move [one's steps], progress'), continuing Old Japanese *pakobu*, attested in the Nihon Shoki and Heian literature.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 運ぶ
Wiktionary — 運ぶ (Japanese)

運べる.etymology: Potential verb ('to be able to carry, can transport'), formed as the regular *e*-grade potential derivative (*hakob-e-ru*) of the consonant-stem (godan) verb 運ぶ (*hakobu* 'to carry, transport').

history.meaning: can carry; be able to transport

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 運ぶ
Wiktionary — 運べる (Japanese)

運転手.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('driver, chauffeur, motorman, operator'), formed from 運転 (うんてん 'operation, driving, revolving movement', from 運 'move, carry' + 転 'revolve, turn') + occupational suffix -手 (-しゅ 'operator, specialist').

history.meaning: vehicle driver; train or tram motorman

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 運転手
Wiktionary — 運転手 (Japanese)

過ぎる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive upper monograde (kami-ichidan) verb ('to pass by, elapse; exceed, go too far'), continuing Old Japanese upper bigrade *sugu* (過ぐ, stem *sugi₁-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, paired with transitive 過ごす (*sugosu*).

history.meaning: pass by; elapse; be excessive; too much

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 過ぎる
Wiktionary — 過ぎる (Japanese)

過ごす.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to spend or pass [time]; overdo'), continuing Old and Heian Japanese *sugusu* / *sugosu*, the transitive counterpart of 過ぎる (*sugiru* < *sugu* 'to pass, elapse').

history.form: すぐす / すごす (過ごす)
history.meaning: let time pass; spend time; exceed

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 過ごす
Wiktionary — 過ごす (Japanese)

道.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('road, street, way, path, route; moral way, art/teaching'), continuing Old Japanese *miti*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; analyzed as honorific prefix 御 (*mi₁-*) + 路 (*ti* 'way, road, direction', preserved in 巷 *chimata* 'crossroads').

history.meaning: road; path; journey; way of conduct

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 道
Wiktionary — 道 (Japanese)

道具箱.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and native Japanese compound noun ('toolbox, kit box'), combining Sino-Japanese 道具 (どうぐ 'tool, implement, utensil', originally Buddhist 'requisites for practicing the Way') + native 箱 (はこ → ばこ with rendaku, 'box, case').

history.meaning: toolbox; box for utensils or supplies

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 道具箱
Wiktionary — 道具箱 (Japanese)

道路.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('road, highway, thoroughfare'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 道路, composed of 道 (どう 'way, thoroughfare') + 路 (ろ 'road, path').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 道路
Wiktionary — 道路 (Japanese)

遠い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('far, distant, remote'), continuing Old Japanese *toposi* (stem *topo-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: far; distant in space or time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 遠い
Wiktionary — 遠い (Japanese)

選ぶ.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to choose, select, elect, sort out'), continuing Old Japanese *erabu* (derived from the simpler verb *eru* 選ぶ / 択る 'to pick out, select'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 選ぶ
Wiktionary — 選ぶ (Japanese)

部屋.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 部 (*he*, 'partition, divided section') with rendaku voicing + 屋 (*ya*, 'roof, chamber, house'), literally 'a partitioned-off chamber'.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 部屋 (Japanese)

部屋番号.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('room number'), combining native 部屋 (へや 'room, chamber') + Sino-Japanese 番号 (ばんごう 'assigned number').

history.form: 部屋番号 (へやばんごう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 番号
Wiktionary — 部屋番号 (Japanese)

郵便屋さん.etymology: Colloquial polite compound noun ('mail carrier, postman; post office'), formed from Meiji Sino-Japanese 郵便 (ゆうびん 'postal service, mail', from 郵 'post-stage relay' + 便 'dispatch, message') + occupational suffix -屋 (-や) + polite suffix -さん.

history.form: 郵便屋さん (ゆうびんやさん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 郵便屋
Wiktionary — 郵便屋さん (Japanese)

配線.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun and suru-verb ('wiring, electrical cabling layout'), formed from 配 (はい 'distribute, arrange, allocate') + 線 (せん 'wire, line').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 配線
Wiktionary — 配線 (Japanese)

配達.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 配 ('distribute, allot') and 達 ('reach, deliver to a destination'), coined for modern postal and goods delivery.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 配達 (Japanese)

重い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('heavy, weighty; serious, grave, sluggish'), continuing Old Japanese *omosi* (stem *omo-*), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 重い
Wiktionary — 重い (Japanese)

野菜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('vegetable, greens'), composed of 野 (や 'field, open country') + 菜 (さい 'edible greens, side dish'). Originally denoting wild edible herbs gathered in the fields, in Modern Japanese it generalized to all cultivated culinary vegetables.

history.meaning: wild edible greens gathered from fields

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 野菜
Wiktionary — 野菜 (Japanese)

野菜スープ.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and Western loanword compound ('vegetable soup'), combining 野菜 (やさい 'vegetable') + スープ (borrowed from English *soup*).

history.form: 野菜スープ (やさいスープ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 野菜
Wiktionary — 野菜 (Japanese)

金具.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('metal fittings, hardware, metal clasp or bracket'), formed from native 金 (かな-, bound combining form of *kane* 'metal') + Sino-Japanese 具 (ぐ 'implement, fitting, tool').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 金具
Wiktionary — 金具 (Japanese)

金属.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('metal'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 金属 ('substances belonging to the category of metal'), composed of 金 (きん 'gold, metal') + 属 (ぞく 'class, category, belong to').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 金属
Wiktionary — 金属 (Japanese)

金曜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('Friday', often short for 金曜日), from Classical Chinese and Buddhist astrological 金曜 ('the planet Venus, Metal-star'), composed of 金 (きん 'metal, Venus') + 曜 (よう 'celestial luminary, day of the week').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 金曜
Wiktionary — 金曜 (Japanese)

金曜日.etymology: Compound of 金曜 ('Venus day', linked to the Five Phases element 金 'metal/gold') and 日 ('day') in the seven-day planetary week.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 金曜日 (Japanese)

金物屋.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('hardware store, ironmonger'), formed from 金物 (かなもの 'metalware, hardware, ironware', from *kana-* 'metal' + 物 'thing, goods') + shop suffix -屋 (-や).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 金物屋
Wiktionary — 金物屋 (Japanese)

金色.etymology: Compound noun ('gold color, golden hue'), read either as hybrid きんいろ (Sino-Japanese 金 *kin* 'gold' + native 色 *iro* 'color') or Sino-Japanese こんじき (from Buddhist Chinese 金色 'golden radiance').

history.form: 金色 (こんじき / きんいろ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 金色
Wiktionary — 金色 (Japanese)

針金.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('wire, metal wire'), attested from the Muromachi and Edo periods, formed from 針 (はり 'needle, pin', or 張る 'to stretch taut') + 金 (かね → がね with rendaku, 'metal').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 針金
Wiktionary — 針金 (Japanese)

鉄.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('iron, steel'), borrowed from Middle Chinese 鉄 / 鐵 (*thet* 'iron'), replacing the older native Japanese poetic/archaic compound *kurogane* (黒金 'black metal').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鉄
Wiktionary — 鉄 (Japanese)

鉛筆.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 鉛 ('lead') and 筆 ('writing brush'), originally referring to leaden styluses in classical Chinese and adopted in Edo-Meiji Japan for Western graphite pencils.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 鉛筆 (Japanese)

鉢.etymology: Early loanword ('bowl, pot, flowerpot, basin; crown of the head'), borrowed via Buddhist Chinese 鉢 (*pat*, shortened from 鉢多羅, transcribing Sanskrit *pātra* 'alms bowl of a Buddhist monk').

history.meaning: bowl; basin; flowerpot; crown of the head

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鉢
Wiktionary — 鉢 (Japanese)

鉢植え.etymology: Hybrid Sino-Japanese and native Japanese compound noun ('potted plant, planting in a pot'), formed from 鉢 (はち 'pot, bowl') + 植え (うえ, nominalized stem of 植える 'to plant').

history.meaning: potted plant; growing a plant in a pot

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鉢植え
Wiktionary — 鉢植え (Japanese)

銀.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('silver'), borrowed from Middle Chinese 銀 (*ngjin* 'silver'), largely replacing the older native Japanese compound *shirogane* (白金 'white metal').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 銀
Wiktionary — 銀 (Japanese)

銅.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun ('copper, bronze'), borrowed from Middle Chinese 銅 (*duwng* 'copper, bronze'), largely replacing the older native Japanese compound *akagane* (赤金 'red metal').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 銅
Wiktionary — 銅 (Japanese)

鋼.etymology: Native Japanese contraction はがね from 刃金 (は 'blade edge' + かね 'metal'), written with the single character 鋼 ('tempered steel').
鋼.notes: Originally denoted the hard carbon-steel edge forged into tools and swords; now used for high-tensile piano wire as well.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 鋼 (Japanese)

鋼鉄.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 鋼鉄 (こうてつ), uniting 鋼 ('hardened steel') and 鉄 ('iron').
鋼鉄.notes: Pairs with single-character native/Sino 鋼 (はがね, 'tempered steel').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 鋼鉄 (Japanese)

鍵.etymology: Native Japanese word *kagi*, related to 鉤 ('hook') from the hooked metal bar used to draw or lift wooden latches in early Japanese doors, later applied to keys and locks.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 鍵 (Japanese)

鍵掛け.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('key rack, key hook; locking with a key'), formed from 鍵 (かぎ 'key, lock') + 掛け (かけ, nominalized stem of 掛ける 'to hang, hook, fasten').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鍵
Wiktionary — 鍵 (Japanese)

鍵盤.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 鍵盤 (けんばん), uniting 鍵 ('key, lock bolt') and 盤 ('flat board, tray').
鍵盤.notes: Used both for the full keyboard of a piano or organ and for individual keys along the row.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 鍵盤 (Japanese)

鍵穴.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('keyhole'), formed from 鍵 (かぎ 'key') + 穴 (あな 'hole, slot').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鍵穴
Wiktionary — 鍵穴 (Japanese)

鏡.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('mirror, looking glass; exemplar/model'), continuing Old Japanese *kagami₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; derived from 影 (*kage₂* / bound stem *kaga-* 'reflection, image, light') + 見 (*mi₁*, nominalized stem of 見る 'to see, look at'), literally 'reflection-viewer'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鏡
Wiktionary — 鏡 (Japanese)

鐘.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read かね, 'bell, gong, chime'), continuing Old Japanese *kane*, attested in the Man'yōshū; identical in origin to 金 (*kane* 'metal, ore'), specialized via metonymy for a large hanging bronze bell struck to sound the hours or temple rituals.

history.meaning: metal; bronze temple bell or gong

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鐘
Wiktionary — 鐘 (Japanese)

長い.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('long [in space or time]'), continuing Old Japanese *nagasi* (stem *naga-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*naga-si*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 長い
Wiktionary — 長い (Japanese)

長さ.etymology: Native Japanese deadjectival noun ('length'), formed from the stem *naga-* of 長い ('long') + nominalizing degree suffix -さ (*-sa*, Old Japanese *-sa*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 長さ
Wiktionary — 長さ (Japanese)

門.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun (read もん, 'gate, portal; school of thought, biological phylum'), borrowed early from Middle Chinese 門 (*mwon* 'two-leaved gate, doorway'), alongside the native reading かど (Old Japanese *kado* 'gate, outer doorway').

history.meaning: double-leaf gate; entrance; family or school

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 門
Wiktionary — 門 (Japanese)

閉じる.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to close, shut [eyes, mouth, book, umbrella, or meeting]'), continuing Old Japanese upper bigrade *todu* (閉づ, stem *todi-* 'to shut, fasten closed').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 閉じる
Wiktionary — 閉じる (Japanese)

閉まる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to close, be shut, be locked'), continuing Old Japanese *simaru* ('to be bound tightly, be fastened shut'), the intransitive counterpart of 閉める / 締める (*shimeru*). Written with 閉 when referring to doors, windows, lids, or shops closing.

history.form: しまる (締まる / 閉まる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 閉まる
Wiktionary — 閉まる (Japanese)

開く.etymology: Native Japanese verb written with 開: read either あく (Old Japanese *aku* 'to come open, become vacant or unobstructed', paired with transitive 開ける *akeru*) or ひらく (Old Japanese *piraku* 'to open wide, unfold, blossom, begin', related to 平 *pira* 'flat, broad').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 開く
Wiktionary — 開く (Japanese)

開ける.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to open [a door, window, or container], unwrap, vacate, make room'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *aku* (開く / 明く, stem *ake₂-*), the transitive counterpart of four-grade 開く (*aku* 'to come open').

history.meaning: open something shut; clear a space

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 開ける
Wiktionary — 開ける (Japanese)

間.etymology: Native Japanese noun written with 間: read あいだ ('space between, interval, gap, during, relationship', continuing Old Japanese *apida*, derived from 合い *api* 'meeting, coming together' + locative/state suffix *-da*), or ま ('space, room, pause, time', continuing Old Japanese *ma*).

history.meaning: interval between two things or times; space; room
space between; interval; while; room; pause

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 間
Wiktionary — 間 (Japanese)

間取り図.etymology: Hybrid architectural compound joining native 間取り (まどり, from 間 'room/bay' + 取り 'arranging') with Sino-Japanese 図 (ず, 'diagram, plan').
間取り図.notes: Traditional Japanese rooms were laid out by tatami-module bays (間 ま), giving 間取り for any floor layout.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 間取り図 (Japanese)

間違い.etymology: Native Japanese compound verbal noun ('mistake, error, fault, discrepancy, accident'), nominalized from the連用形 of 間違う (*machigau* 'to differ in interval or alignment, go amiss, make a mistake').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 間違い
Wiktionary — 間違い (Japanese)

間違う.etymology: Native Japanese compound verb ('to make a mistake, be mistaken, go wrong'), attested from the Edo period, formed from 間 (ま 'interval, space, timing') + 違う (ちがう 'to differ, cross at odds, be out of alignment').

history.meaning: be out of alignment; make a mistake; err

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 間違う
Wiktionary — 間違う (Japanese)

間違える.etymology: Native Japanese compound transitive verb ('to mistake [one thing for another], make an error in, confuse'), formed as the lower-bigrade/ichidan transitive counterpart of 間違う (*machigau*), from 間 (ま 'interval, timing') + 違える (ちがえる 'to alter, cross, miss').

history.meaning: mistake one thing for another; make an error

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 間違える
Wiktionary — 間違える (Japanese)

防ぐ.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to defend against, ward off, prevent, keep out'), continuing Old Japanese *puseku* / *pusegu*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Nihon Shoki; cognate with 塞ぐ (*fusagu* 'to block up, close off, obstruct').

history.form: ふせく / ふせぐ (防ぐ)
history.meaning: block off; hold back; defend against

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 防ぐ
Wiktionary — 防ぐ (Japanese)

降りる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive upper monograde (kami-ichidan) verb ('to descend, go down, step down; get off [a vehicle]'), continuing Old Japanese upper bigrade *oru* (下る / 降る, stem *ori-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, paired with transitive 降ろす / 下ろす (*orosu*).

history.form: おる (降る / 下る, upper bigrade)
history.meaning: come down from a height; descend
go down; descend; get off (a train, bus, or stairs)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 降りる
Wiktionary — 降りる (Japanese)

降る.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to fall from the sky [of rain, snow, hail, ash]'), continuing Old Japanese *puru* (four-grade *pur-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: fall from the sky (of rain or snow)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 降る
Wiktionary — 降る (Japanese)

陶器.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 陶 ('kiln-fired pottery, mould clay') and 器 ('vessel, implement'), designating glazed earthenware and stoneware vessels.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 陶器 (Japanese)

陽翔.etymology: Modern Japanese male given name (commonly read はると or ひろと), combining 陽 ('sun, sunlight, bright warmth') + 翔 ('soar, fly high').

history.form: 陽翔 (はると / ひろと)
history.meaning: male given name ('soaring in the sunlight')

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 陽
Wiktionary — 陽 (Japanese)

隅.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('corner, nook, inside angle'), continuing Old Japanese *sumi₁*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隅
Wiktionary — 隅 (Japanese)

隆.etymology: Japanese male given name (read たかし), written with the single kanji 隆 ('prosperous, rising high, flourishing, noble'), read with the native Japanese adjective *takashi* (高し 'high, lofty, noble').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隆
Wiktionary — 隆 (Japanese)

階.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and counter ('story, floor [of a building]; stairs, rank'), borrowed from Middle Chinese 階 (*kɛj* 'steps leading up to a hall, tier, story, rank').

history.meaning: floor/story of a building; stair; rank

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 階
Wiktionary — 階 (Japanese)

階段.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('stairs, staircase, stairway, steps'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 階段, composed of 階 (かい 'steps, tier') + 段 (だん 'step, level, stage').

history.meaning: steps leading up to a hall

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 階段
Wiktionary — 階段 (Japanese)

隠し扉.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('hidden door, secret door'), formed from 隠し (かくし, stem of 隠す 'to hide, conceal') + 扉 (とびら 'hinged door, door leaf', from 戸 *to* 'door' + 枚 *hira* 'flat panel').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 扉
Wiktionary — 扉 (Japanese)

隠す.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to hide, conceal, cover up, keep secret'), continuing Old Japanese *kakusu*, the transitive counterpart of 隠る / 隠れる (*kakuru* / *kakureru* 'to hide oneself, be hidden').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隠す
Wiktionary — 隠す (Japanese)

隠れる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to hide oneself, be hidden, disappear from view'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *kakuru* (隠る, stem *kakure-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū (alongside older four-grade *kakuru*).

history.meaning: go out of sight; hide oneself; pass away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隠れる
Wiktionary — 隠れる (Japanese)

隣.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('next door, neighbor, adjoining house or space'), continuing Old Japanese *tonari*, attested in the Man'yōshū; traditionally analyzed as 戸並み / 戸連り (*to-nari* 'doors lined up side by side', from 戸 *to* 'door, house' + *nari* / 並 'in a row').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隣
Wiktionary — 隣 (Japanese)

雇う.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to employ, hire, engage for wages'), continuing Old Japanese *yatopu*, attested in the Nihon Shoki and Heian texts (originally 'to ask someone from another household to lend labor', traditionally analyzed as 家 *ya* 'house' + 問ふ *topu* 'to ask, call upon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 雇う
Wiktionary — 雇う (Japanese)

離れる.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to separate, part from, move away, become detached'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *panaru* (離る, stem *panare-*), the intransitive counterpart of 離す / 放す (*hanasu* 'to separate, let go').

history.meaning: part from; become separated or distant

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 離れる
Wiktionary — 離れる (Japanese)

雨.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('rain'), continuing Old Japanese *ame₂* (alternating with bound prefix *ama-* in compounds like 雨戸 *amado* and 雨漏り *amamori*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*amai* ('rain').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 雨
Wiktionary — 雨 (Japanese)

雨上がり.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('after the rain, clearing up after rain'), formed from 雨 (あめ 'rain') + 上がり (あがり, nominalized stem of 上がる 'to rise, stop/clear up [of rain]').

history.form: 雨上がり (あめあがり / あまあがり)
history.meaning: just after the rain has stopped

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 雨上がり
Wiktionary — 雨上がり (Japanese)

雨戸.etymology: Transparent native Japanese (和語) compound joining あま- (the bound combining form of 雨 あめ, 'rain') and 戸 (と, 'door, sliding shutter').
雨戸.notes: Traditional exterior wooden storm shutters that slide or swing closed to protect glass or paper windows from wind and rain.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 雨戸 (Japanese)

雨漏り.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun ('roof leak, rainwater leaking through a ceiling'), formed from the bound stem *ama-* of 雨 ('rain') + 漏り (もり, nominalized stem of 漏る 'to leak, drip through').

history.meaning: leaking of rainwater through a roof

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 雨漏り
Wiktionary — 雨漏り (Japanese)

雨粒.etymology: Native Japanese compound of あま- (bound form of 雨 あめ, 'rain') and 粒 (つぶ, 'round drop, grain, bead').
雨粒.notes: Shares the older combining vowel あま- seen in 雨戸 ('storm shutter') and 雨傘 ('umbrella').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 雨粒 (Japanese)

電気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('electricity; electric light'), composed of 電 (でん 'lightning, flash') + 気 (き 'vital energy, vapor, force'). Adopted in late Edo and early Meiji science to render Western *electricity*, and in everyday spoken Japanese also used metonymically for electric light.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 電気
Wiktionary — 電気 (Japanese)

電球.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('electric light bulb'), coined in the Meiji period from 電 (でん 'electricity, electric') + 球 (きゅう 'sphere, globe, bulb').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 電球
Wiktionary — 電球 (Japanese)

電線.etymology: Sino-Japanese Meiji compound of 電 ('electricity, lightning') and 線 ('thread, wire, line'), created for telegraph and electrical power wiring.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 電線 (Japanese)

電話.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese coinage (wasei-kango) combining 電 ('lightning, electricity') and 話 ('speech, conversation') to translate English telephone.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 電話 (Japanese)

電話番号.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('telephone number'), combining 電話 (でんわ 'telephone') + 番号 (ばんごう 'assigned number').

history.form: 電話番号 (でんわばんごう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 電話番号
Wiktionary — 電話番号 (Japanese)

電車.etymology: Modern Sino-Japanese compound of 電 ('electricity') and 車 ('wheeled vehicle, carriage'), coined for electric streetcars and commuter trains.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 電車 (Japanese)

震える.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to tremble, shiver, shake, quiver'), continuing Heian–Middle Japanese lower bigrade *furufu* (震ふ / 振ふ), the intransitive/spontaneous counterpart of four-grade 振るう (*furuu* < *purupu* 'to shake, brandish', iterative of 振る *furu*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 震える
Wiktionary — 震える (Japanese)

青.etymology: Native Japanese color noun ('blue, green, blue-green; unripe, pale'), continuing Old Japanese *awo*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, where it covered the cool-color spectrum between bright white (*siro*), red (*aka*), and dark black (*kuro*)—encompassing the sky, sea, green vegetation, and pale gray horses.

history.meaning: blue-green-gray cool color; green foliage; blue sky/sea
blue; green (in traffic lights, vegetation); unripeness

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 青
Wiktionary — 青 (Japanese)

青い.etymology: Native Japanese color adjective ('blue, green; pale; unripe, inexperienced'), continuing Old Japanese *awosi* (stem *awo-*), derived from the color noun 青 (*awo*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 青い
Wiktionary — 青い (Japanese)

静か.etymology: Native Japanese na-adjective built from the ancient root *sidu-* ('calm, settled, sunken', also seen in 沈む *shizumu*, 'sink, settle') plus the descriptive suffix *-ka*.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 静か (Japanese)

静けさ.etymology: Native Japanese deadjectival noun ('quietness, stillness, silence, tranquility'), formed from the stem *shizuke-* of the classical adjective 静けし (*shizukeshi*, Old Japanese *sidukesi* 'calm, still, quiet') + nominalizing degree suffix -さ (*-sa*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 静けさ
Wiktionary — 静けさ (Japanese)

革.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('leather, hide, tanned skin'), continuing Old Japanese *kapa* ('skin, hide, bark'), sharing the same native etymon as 皮 (*kawa*) and orthographically specialized with the character 革 ('depilated and cured animal hide') for tanned leather.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 革
Wiktionary — 革 (Japanese)

靴.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('shoes, boots, footwear'), continuing Old Japanese *kutu*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Nihon Shoki for enclosed footwear.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 靴
Wiktionary — 靴 (Japanese)

鞄.etymology: Early modern loanword ('bag, satchel, briefcase, suitcase'), attested from the late Edo and early Meiji periods (likely borrowed from a Chinese dialectal reading of 夾板 'wooden document-carrying boards/portfolio' or Dutch *kabas* 'handbag, basket'), and assigned the character 鞄 ('leatherworker, leather bag') in the Meiji period.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 鞄
Wiktionary — 鞄 (Japanese)

音.etymology: Native Japanese noun written with 音: read おと ('sound, noise, report, news', continuing Old Japanese *oto₂*) or ね ('musical tone, note, bird or insect cry', continuing Old Japanese *ne*), as well as Sino-Japanese おん / いん (from Middle Chinese 音 *'jim*).

history.meaning: sound, noise, rumor / musical tone, cry

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 音
Wiktionary — 音 (Japanese)

音楽.etymology: Sino-Japanese word borrowed from Middle Chinese 音樂 ('music'), built from 音 ('sound') and 楽 (old form 樂, 'music; enjoyment').

sources.title: Wiktionary — 音楽 (Japanese)

音符.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 音 ('sound, tone') and 符 ('tally mark, written symbol'), literally 'a symbol marking a musical pitch and duration'.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 音符 (Japanese)

音階.etymology: Sino-Japanese musical compound noun ('musical scale'), coined in the Meiji period to translate English *scale* / German *Tonleiter*, from 音 (おん 'sound, musical note') + 階 (かい 'steps, ladder, gradations').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 音階
Wiktionary — 音階 (Japanese)

音響.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('acoustics, sound, echo, reverberation'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 音響 ('sound and its echo'), composed of 音 (おん 'sound') + 響 (きょう 'echo, resonance, reverberation').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 音響
Wiktionary — 音響 (Japanese)

響き.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('echo, reverberation, resonance, sound, ring'), nominalized from the連用形 of 響く (*hibiku*, Old Japanese *pibiku* 'to resound, echo, vibrate').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 響き
Wiktionary — 響き (Japanese)

響く.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to resound, echo, reverberate, vibrate; affect'), continuing Old Japanese *pibiku*, attested in the Man'yōshū and Nihon Shoki.

history.meaning: echo; resound; reverberate; have an effect on

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 響く
Wiktionary — 響く (Japanese)

頃.etymology: Native Japanese noun and temporal suffix ('approximate time, about, around; right time or season'), continuing Old Japanese *koro₂*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; related to the root *koro* ('revolving cycle of time').

history.meaning: span or point of time; season
approximate time; around; about; opportune moment

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頃
Wiktionary — 頃 (Japanese)

預かる.etymology: Native Japanese verb ('to take into one's custody, keep in trust, look after, take charge of'), continuing Old Japanese *adukaru* ('to be entrusted with, have a share in'), paired with transitive 預ける (*azukeru*).

history.meaning: be entrusted with; have a part in
keep in custody; look after; take charge of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 預かる
Wiktionary — 預かる (Japanese)

預ける.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to deposit, entrust, leave in someone's care or custody'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *aduku* (預く, stem *aduke₂-*), the transitive counterpart of 預かる (*azukaru*).

history.meaning: deposit; leave in someone's care; entrust

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 預ける
Wiktionary — 預ける (Japanese)

頑丈.etymology: Sino-Japanese adjectival noun ('sturdy, solid, robust, strongly built'), reshaped in the Edo period by initial voicing (*k-* > *g-*) and folk-etymological re-spelling with 頑 ('stubborn, hard') from medieval 巌乗 / 強盛 (*kanjō* / *ganjō* 'solidly built, firm and unyielding').

history.form: かんじゃう → がんじゃう (巌乗 / 頑丈)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頑丈
Wiktionary — 頑丈 (Japanese)

頑固.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and adjectival noun ('stubborn, obstinate, headstrong, persistent'), borrowed from Classical Chinese 頑固, composed of 頑 (がん 'thick-headed, obstinate, unyielding') + 固 (こ 'firm, hard, fixed').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頑固
Wiktionary — 頑固 (Japanese)

領収書.etymology: Sino-Japanese commercial compound noun ('receipt, voucher acknowledging payment'), combining 領収 (りょうしゅう 'receiving and taking into possession', from 領 'receive, take charge' + 収 'collect, take in') + 書 (しょ 'document, certificate').

history.form: 領収書 (りょうしゅうしょ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 領収書
Wiktionary — 領収書 (Japanese)

頭.etymology: Native Japanese noun (read あたま or かしら, 'head; hair; mind/brain; leader, top'), continuing Heian Japanese *atama* (originally denoting the fontanelle or top crown of the skull, before displacing the older general word *kashira* / *kaburi* 'head' in everyday speech).

history.meaning: top crown of the skull; fontanelle

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頭
Wiktionary — 頭 (Japanese)

頭文字.etymology: Hybrid native and Sino-Japanese compound noun ('initial letter, capital letter, acronym'), formed from native 頭 (かしら 'head, top, beginning') + Sino-Japanese 文字 (もじ 'letter, character').

history.meaning: first character of a word or verse; initial letter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頭文字
Wiktionary — 頭文字 (Japanese)

頼む.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to request, ask a favor, entrust, rely on'), continuing Old Japanese *tanomu* (attested in the Man'yōshū both as four-grade 'to rely upon, trust in' and lower bigrade 'to cause someone to rely on one').

history.meaning: rely upon; trust in; count on
ask a favor; request; entrust; rely on

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頼む
Wiktionary — 頼む (Japanese)

頼もしい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective ('reliable, trustworthy, dependable, promising'), continuing Heian Japanese *tanomosi*, derived from the verb 頼む (*tanomu* 'to rely on, trust') + adjectival suffix *-shii*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 頼もしい
Wiktionary — 頼もしい (Japanese)

題名.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound noun ('title [of a book, play, song, or artwork]'), formed from 題 (だい 'forehead; heading, subject, inscription') + 名 (めい 'name').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 題名
Wiktionary — 題名 (Japanese)

額.etymology: As native Japanese ひたい ('forehead, brow'), continuing Old Japanese *pitapi*, attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū (related to 直向ひ *pita-mukapi* 'facing directly forward'); as Sino-Japanese がく ('framed picture, inscribed plaque; amount/sum of money'), from Middle Chinese 額 (*ngæk* 'forehead; inscribed plaque hung over a gate; fixed quota/sum').

history.meaning: forehead / picture frame, plaque; sum of money

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 額
Wiktionary — 額 (Japanese)

顔.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('face, countenance, look, expression; reputation'), continuing Old Japanese *kapo*, attested in the Man'yōshū, where it originally meant 'overall outward appearance, look, or air' (while 面 *omo* / *omote* meant the physical face) before shifting in the Heian period to become the primary word for 'face'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 顔
Wiktionary — 顔 (Japanese)

風.etymology: Native Japanese noun ('wind, breeze, draught; cold/illness; manner'), continuing Old Japanese *kaze* (alternating with bound prefix *kaza-* in compounds like 風見 *kazami*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*kasai*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 風
Wiktionary — 風 (Japanese)

飛ぶ.etymology: Native Japanese intransitive verb ('to fly, soar; jump, leap; scatter'), continuing Old Japanese *to₂bu* (four-grade *to₂b-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*tənpu*.

history.meaning: fly; jump; be blown away; skip

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 飛ぶ
Wiktionary — 飛ぶ (Japanese)

食べる.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to eat; live on'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade *tabu* (食ぶ / 給ぶ, stem *tabe-*), a contracted variant of *tamapu* (給ふ / 賜ふ 'to receive humbly from a superior, partake of food or drink bestowed'). Originally a humble verb meaning 'humbly partake of food or drink', it bleached in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese into the standard everyday verb for 'to eat'.

history.meaning: humbly receive food or drink from a superior

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 食べる
Wiktionary — 食べる (Japanese)

飲む.etymology: Native Japanese transitive verb ('to drink, swallow, take [medicine], smoke'), continuing Old Japanese *no₂mu* (four-grade *no₂m-*), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, from Proto-Japonic *\*nəmu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 飲む
Wiktionary — 飲む (Japanese)

香ばしい.etymology: Native Japanese adjective (read こうばしい or かんばしい, 'fragrant, aromatic, savory [especially of roasted or toasted foods]'), continuing Heian *kaubasi* < Old Japanese *kagupasi* (香ぐはし 'having a fine scent, fragrant'), a compound of 香 (*ka* 'scent, aroma') + 細し / 詳し (*kupasi* > *-guwashi* 'fine, delicate, lovely').

history.form: かうばし / かんばし

history.meaning: savory and aromatic (of roasted grain, tea, or baking)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 香ばしい
Wiktionary — 香ばしい (Japanese)

香り.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('fragrance, aroma, scent, perfume'), nominalized from the連用形 of 香る / 薫る (*kaoru* < Old Japanese *kaworu* 'to emit a fragrance or mist', derived from 香 *ka* 'scent, smell').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 香り
Wiktionary — 香り (Japanese)

駄目.etymology: Compound noun and adjectival noun ('no good, useless, in vain, forbidden, hopeless'), originating as a technical term in the board game Go (囲碁) for neutral intersections between black and white territories that yield zero points to either player: from 駄 (だ 'worthless, mere packhorse load') + 目 (め 'point or intersection on a Go board'). Generalized in Edo-period speech to 'useless, fruitless, not allowed'.

history.meaning: neutral point of no value on a Go board
useless; no good; in vain; forbidden

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 駄目
Wiktionary — 駄目 (Japanese)

駅.etymology: From Sino-Japanese 駅 (traditional 驛, eki), which in the ancient Ritsuryō highway system named post-horse relay stations spaced along imperial roads; in the Meiji railway era it was adopted for train stations.

sources.title: Wiktionary — 駅 (Japanese)

駆け込む.etymology: Native Japanese compound intransitive verb ('to run into, rush into, dash in [especially seeking refuge or just before a deadline]'), formed from 駆け (かけ, stem of 駆ける 'to run, gallop, dash') + 込む (こむ 'to go into, enter').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 駆け込む
Wiktionary — 駆け込む (Japanese)

騒ぎ.etymology: Native Japanese verbal noun ('uproar, commotion, tumult, fuss, disturbance'), nominalized from the連用形 of 騒ぐ (*sawagu*, Old Japanese *sawaku* 'to make a clamor, be agitated, bustle').
